trackers.why: src/analytics/index.ts: Analytics.track wraps PostHog capture(event, {...defaultMetadata, ...walletContext, ...params}). Event names are analytics.event.* / event.* constants from src/analytics/event.ts. Used from ~150 files.
src/analytics/index.ts: Analytics.identify calls PostHog identify(deviceId, {walletAddressHash, walletType, ...userProperties}); the id is the device id, the argument is traits only.

src/__swaps__/utils/trackSwapEvent.ts: second-level wrapper. The caller passes the event constant (swapsSubmitted or swapsFailed) as arg 0. The wrapper builds every property itself from the swaps store and the call's parameters, then calls analytics.track(event, params).

Every file imports the instance as a named export (`import { analytics } from '@/analytics'`, e.g. Chart.tsx:14). The earlier entry with `from` didn't match that import shape, so this one matches `analytics.track` by its callee alone. src/analytics/index.ts:102 is `track(event, params, walletContext)`, which sends the PostHog `capture`.
Same named-instance import as above. src/analytics/index.ts:77 `identify(userProperties)` calls `client.identify(deviceId, traits)`. Chart.tsx:271 and :282 pass traits such as `{ chartType }`.

src/analytics/index.ts exports `analytics = new Analytics()`, a named export holding an instance, not an SDK default or namespace import. This entry has no `from`, so it matches `analytics.track(...)` by name in case the `from: "@/analytics"` entry doesn't match the named-export instance. That entry matched none of the calls above, which are flagged as vendor SDK calls outside a wrapper.
src/analytics/index.ts:91 `screen(route, params)` sends a PostHog screen event named by a Routes value. Callers pass the route constant, so the scanner may read it from Routes.

src/analytics/index.ts identify(userProperties) sends them as PostHog person traits via client.identify(deviceId, {...metadata, ...userProperties}); callers like src/features/positions/stores/positionsStore.ts:167 and src/features/rnbw-membership/stores/rnbwMembershipAnalyticsStore.ts:41 use it only to set profile properties (positionsAmount, stakedRnbw, rnbwMembershipTier)

src/analytics/index.ts exports `analytics = new Analytics()` (a named-import class instance, wrapping PostHog.capture). The `from: @/analytics` entry did not match member calls on that named import, so every analytics.track(...) was still flagged as a vendor SDK call. This entry matches the call by its text.

src/analytics/index.ts Analytics.identify wraps PostHog.identify(deviceId, traits). src/hooks/useIdentifyAppIcon.ts:10 calls analytics.identify({ appIcon }) and was flagged as a vendor SDK call for the same reason as analytics.track.
src/analytics/index.ts defines screen(route, params) which calls PostHog screen; src/navigation/onNavigationStateChange.js:130 calls it with the route name

src/analytics/index.ts exports `analytics` as a named export (a Analytics class instance), so the scanner isn't matching the named import against `from`. This entry matches `analytics.track` as written in code, and the callers' own flagged lines (wallet.ts, settings.ts, notifications/analytics.ts) read it. track() wraps posthog capture and always adds walletAddressHash and walletType.

src/analytics/index.ts Analytics.identify(userProperties) calls posthog identify(deviceId, traits). Same named-export reason as analytics.track, and it covers notifications/analytics.ts:24,118 and redux/settings.ts:115.

findings.title: Raw wallet addresses and ENS names sent as event properties, bypassing the wallet-address hash
findings.explanation: The wrapper attaches only `walletAddressHash` to every event, so the design avoids sending plain addresses. These import-flow events send the user's plain address, ENS or Unstoppable name (`address`, `addressOrEnsName`, `input`, `ens`) as event properties. `input` can be whatever the user typed into the import field. When the user pasted a seed phrase, `input` is the sanitized seed phrase, but the plain-address events in this file (watchWallet, showWalletProfileModalForReadOnlyWallet) only reach it for address inputs. These properties tie an analytics profile to a public identity and to watched wallets. The values are also unbounded and have high cardinality.
findings.fix: Stop sending address, ENS name and raw input. Send a hashed address, a boolean such as `is_ens` or `input_type = ens | unstoppable | address | seed`, and the existing `type`. Dropping the properties changes the existing events' schema, so add the properties as new fields or events, deprecate the old ones with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: useImportingWallet.ts:163-173, 193-203, 222-225, 233-236, 271-274, 279-282 - These calls send the plain address, the ENS or Unstoppable name, and the typed `input`, even though the wrapper already adds a hash. One correction: watchWallet is not limited to address inputs. In the derive branch, line 273 sends `address: input`, which can be a seed phrase (see F5).

findings.title: Raw token-search text is sent as an event property
findings.explanation: The raw text the user typed into the swap and Discover token searches is sent as `query`. The swap token lists send the full `searchQuery` on `swapsSearchedForToken`. `tokenList` sends `query` from both the swap search hook and Discover search. The Discover search input sends `query` together with `length` on `searchQuery`. Search text is free user input and can contain pasted addresses or ENS names, which can be linked to a wallet because every event also carries `walletAddressHash`. The design rules say to send `char_count` and `result_count`, never the query. `length` is already sent next to the raw query on `searchQuery`.
findings.fix: Drop `query` from all three events and send `char_count` plus `result_count`. If a query is needed to debug empty results, send only a flag such as `looks_like_address`. This removes a property from existing events, so give it a SEMANTICS changelog line. The property is additive removal and does not break the event names.
findings.verifier_note: DiscoverSearch.tsx:111 sends `query: searchQueryForSearch`. The registry also documents `query` on swaps.searched_for_token and on Search Query - The raw search text is sent, and `length` already sits next to it on Search Query.

findings.title: Free-text and user-entered values are sent as event properties
findings.explanation: `tappedDoneEditingWallet` sends the label the user typed for their wallet as `wallet_label`. `viewedProfile` sends the ENS name of the viewed profile as `name`, which identifies another person's wallet. `claimClaimableFailed` sends the raw `e.message` from the provider or signer as `errorMessage`. That text is unbounded and can contain addresses, calldata or RPC URLs. The design rules say never to send raw user text or identity values as event properties. Send lengths, booleans or enum codes instead.
findings.fix: Replace `wallet_label` with `has_label` or `char_count`. Replace the ENS `name` with `is_own_profile` or `has_ens`. Replace `errorMessage` with a mapped `failure_reason` enum. Removing or renaming these properties changes existing events: add the new property alongside, stop sending the old one after a dual-send window, and mark the old property deprecated in the registry.
findings.verifier_note: ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:264 sends `wallet_label: name`, ProfileSheet.tsx:71 sends the ENS `name`, and Airdrops/utils.ts:139/155 sends the raw `e.message` as errorMessage - All three are free text or identity values.

findings.title: swaps.submitted also fires after a 'handled' failure, so one attempt can count as failed and submitted
findings.explanation: When `errorMessage` is set, `swapsFailed` is tracked. The branch only returns for non-'handled' errors, so for 'handled' the code falls through to the recent-swap and sheet-dismissal code. It then reaches `trackSwapEvent(swapsSubmitted)`. The swap funnel, the submitted count and the failure rate are all affected. The registry description flags this as unconfirmed, and the code confirms it. On this path `swaps.submitted` carries `errorMessage = null`, which is wrong for that attempt.
findings.fix: Return after tracking `swapsFailed` in the 'handled' case, or only track submitted when `errorMessage` is falsy. This changes the firing moment of a core money event, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line with the date. Tell analysts that counts on 'handled' errors will drop.
findings.verifier_note: swap-provider.tsx:337-362. The `return` only happens inside `errorMessage !== 'handled'`, so a 'handled' error falls through to line 396 and sends swapsSubmitted. trackSwapEvent.ts:49 then sets errorMessage to null.

findings.title: Raw input (possibly a seed phrase or private key) is sent as `address` on watch_wallet
findings.explanation: In the last branch of handlePressImportButton, the input is not an ENS name, an Unstoppable domain or a valid 0x address. It is whatever deriveAccountFromWalletInput accepts, which includes seed phrases and private keys. The watch_wallet call sends `address: input`, the raw sanitized text, even though the derived `walletResult.address` is available. If someone pastes a secret into the watch flow, the secret goes to analytics. The registry description for `address` ('the raw input otherwise') confirms this path.
findings.fix: In this branch send `walletResult.address` (or nothing) instead of `input`. Never send raw input. This changes the meaning of `address` on the existing event, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line. The change only removes secret material, so no dual-fire is needed.
findings.verifier_note: useImportingWallet.ts:245-274. The last branch accepts anything deriveAccountFromWalletInput takes, and with type 'watch' it sends `address: input`, the sanitized raw text, even though `walletResult.address` is available. Whether the watch screen lets someone paste a secret is a UI question, but the code path exists.

findings.title: Raw decoded QR content is sent as an event property
items: Scanned broken or unsupported QR code
findings.explanation: handleScanInvalid sends the full decoded text of any QR code the app can't recognise as `qrCodeData`. This event fires only for content the app doesn't understand, so it is arbitrary third-party content. It could be a URL with tokens, contact details, a payment request, or a QR code of someone's seed phrase or private key. The design rules say never to send raw user text. Send lengths or buckets instead.
findings.fix: Stop sending the raw string. Send `char_count` and a coarse `content_kind` bucket instead (for example url, hex_string, other, computed locally). Optionally add `error_reason`. Removing `qrCodeData` changes the event's schema, but it only drops data. Keep the event name, and mark `qrCodeData` as deprecated in the registry. Also confirm that the analytics project does not already hold values that need purging.
findings.verifier_note: The registry entry and event type show that handleScanInvalid sends `qrCodeData`, the full decoded payload, for any unrecognised QR code.

findings.title: User-typed wallet group name is sent as an event property
findings.explanation: On submit, `addNewWalletGroupName` sends `name: value.trim()`, the free text the user typed into the wallet-group input. Raw user text is on the 'never send' list. People name groups after themselves, family members or institutions. The event schema declares `name: string`, so this is deliberate rather than an accident.
findings.fix: Drop `name` and send `char_count` instead, or send nothing, since the question is only how many groups get created. Changing the schema alters an existing event, so keep the event name. Note in the registry that older rows carry names, and consider purging them from the analytics tool.
findings.verifier_note: The registry entry and the cited lines show `name: value.trim()`, raw user text, sent on submit.

findings.title: Money and on-chain outcomes are split into separate `*Failed` events instead of one event with `status`
findings.explanation: Each money flow (place order, deposit, withdrawal, redeem, rewards claim, airdrop claim, stake, unstake) has a success event and a separate `_failed` event. Conversion rates and funnels need a union of the two, and a funnel on the success event silently drops the failures. The failure events carry free-text `errorMessage` (`error.message`) and no normalised `failure_reason`, so failures can't be grouped. In the airdrop and rewards claim success events, `status` is the backend's final status and not a fixed success/failed value. Order failures are also tracked in two places. The sheet's catch block fires `predictionsPlaceOrderFailed` (buy and sell), and the executor separately fires `predictionsOrderMatchFailed`. These two events may describe the same failed order.
findings.fix: Don't rename in place. Add `status = success | failed | cancelled` and a normalised `failure_reason` to the outcome events. Keep the `_failed` events during a dual-fire window, then mark them `deprecated` with `replaced_by`. Write a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line, because money events are core and sit on dashboards. Replace `errorMessage` with a bounded `failure_reason` enum. Decide whether `predictionsOrderMatchFailed` is a separate stage or a duplicate of the order failure, and document it.
findings.verifier_note: The registry has separate success and `.failed` entries for place_order, redeem, withdraw, rnbw claims, stake and unstake. The failed events carry free-text errorMessage, and PolymarketNewPositionSheet.tsx:209 sends place_order.failed separately from order_match.failed - This is the rule-4 split.

findings.title: Cash outcomes are split into separate *_Failed events instead of a status on one outcome event
findings.explanation: Each flow sends a success event and a separate failure event. Examples: buy order completed/failed, KYC approved/failed, card linked/link-failed, phone verified/verify-failed, sign-in succeeded/failed/cancelled. Every conversion rate therefore needs a union of events, and funnels drop the failures. Rule 4 says failure belongs on the outcome event as `status` (success, failed, cancelled) plus `failure_reason`. The failure properties are also inconsistent. `cashBuyOrderFailed` sends `failureReason` and `errorCode` in camelCase. The KYC, phone and card events send `reason`. Sign-in cancellation is already a separate event, which fits the `cancelled` status value.
findings.fix: Add the outcome events with `status` and `failure_reason`, and use one property vocabulary. Don't rename in place. Deprecate the old `*Failed` events with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire the money events (buy order) and KYC events for one release (`dual_fire_until`). Add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: cashBuyOrderStore.ts:123 and :146 are separate completed and failed events. The failure properties are named inconsistently: `failureReason`/`errorCode` here, `reason` on the other cash events.

findings.title: Failure events are split from outcomes and miss several failure and cancel paths in the cash flows
findings.explanation: Each cash step has a success event and a separate `*_failed` event, instead of one outcome event with `status` and `failure_reason`. Every conversion rate then needs a union of events. The failure events also fire only on some paths. In `useAddPasskeyFlow.submit`, access refusal, passkey cancellation and 'already on device' all return before `cashPasskeyFailed`, and there is no `cancelled` signal. In `useWalletLinkFlow`, `WalletSignatureError` and handled errors return silently. In `advanceToChallenge`, access refusal returns without tracking. Funnels from submitted to added therefore show drop-off that is really cancellation or refusal, and the failure counts understate what happened. The same code logs through `logger.error` on exactly the paths that do get an event.
findings.fix: Move to one outcome event per step (for example `cash_passkey_completed`) with `status = success | failed | cancelled` and `failure_reason`. Treat cancelled as not a failure. This is a rename, so go through deprecate + `replaced_by` and dual-fire the old events for one release, with cut-over by app version. Until then, document in the registry which paths emit no event.
findings.verifier_note: useAddPasskeyFlow.ts:59-71. A cash-access refusal, a passkey cancellation and a passkey already on the device all return before cashPasskeyFailed (line 73), so those paths send no event.

findings.title: Backup events: 'skipped password' fires on any keychain error, and event names are inconsistent
items: Didn't save backup password on iCloud
findings.explanation: `saveBackupPassword` tracks 'Didn't save backup password' in the catch block, so any keychain failure is counted as the user skipping. A skip and a failure are different things. Backup success and failure are also split across `Backup Complete` and `backup.error`. The names mix three styles: Title Case (`Backup Complete`), free text with quotes (`Tapped "Confirm Backup"`) and dotted lower case (`backup.error`). Breakdowns and searches by name are awkward, and the generic `category` and `label` properties repeat constants.
findings.fix: Add a `status` or `failure_reason` to the password event, or track the catch separately as a failure. Don't rename in place. Introduce `object_action` snake_case events, deprecate the old names with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire `Backup Complete` for one release because it is a core event.
findings.verifier_note: backup.ts:529-536. Any throw from setSharedWebCredentials sends backupSkippedPassword with no reason, so failures are counted as skips.

findings.title: Perps failures are separate `_failed` events instead of `status`/`failure_reason` on the outcome event, and carry raw error text
findings.explanation: Close position, create trigger order and cancel trigger order each emit one success event and a separate failure event from the catch branch. Every conversion rate for these money-adjacent flows needs a union of two events, and funnels drop the failures. The failure events send `errorMessage`, which is the free-text string from `parseHyperliquidErrorMessage`, not a bounded enum, so it can't be broken down cleanly.
findings.fix: Add `status = success | failed` and a bounded `failure_reason` to the outcome events (`perps_position_closed`, `perps_trigger_order_created`, `perps_trigger_order_canceled`). Map the Hyperliquid error to an enum and mark values you haven't seen `(UNCONFIRMED)`. Don't rename in place: keep the old `*Failed` events as deprecated with `replaced_by` and dual-fire for one release, because they sit on perps dashboards.
findings.verifier_note: The registry shows separate perps `*.failed` events carrying the output of parseHyperliquidErrorMessage. The close and cancel calls I read (ClosePositionBottomSheet.tsx:179, TriggerOrdersSection.tsx:71) match.

findings.title: token_created fires before the rest of the launch can fail, so one launch can count as both created and failed
findings.explanation: token_created is sent as soon as launchToken returns, but the same try block then awaits publicClient.getTransaction. If that call throws, the catch branch sends token_launcher.creation_failed for a coin that was created. Failure is also modelled as three separate events (creation_failed, image_upload_failed, wallet_load_failed) instead of status and failure_reason on one outcome event (rule R004). Any launch success rate then needs a union, and the double-fired launches inflate both sides. share_pressed also fires after the share sheet closes whether or not the person shared, so it counts opened sheets, not shares.
findings.fix: Move the token_created call so it fires after the part that can still fail, or send it with status and put failures on the same outcome event with failure_reason. Because this changes the firing moment, add a changelog line starting SEMANTICS:. Add the failure form of the event first, then deprecate the _failed events with replaced_by and dual-fire for one release. Don't delete or rename them in place. Say in the share_pressed description that it fires when the sheet closes, not on a completed share.
findings.verifier_note: tokenLauncherStore.ts:379 tracks token_created, then lines 386 and 417 (getTransaction, addNewTransaction) run in the same try, and the catch at 438 sends creation_failed. The share_pressed point is confirmed by TokenLauncherFooter.tsx:203-212.

findings.title: Wallet creation and backup failures are separate events with free-text error values
findings.explanation: Wallet creation uses a success event and a failure event. The failure event's `error` is a mix of fixed codes ('wallet_or_address_missing', 'wallet_already_exists') and raw `error.message` text. The raw text splits any breakdown into many buckets. Backup failure is split into one event per cloud platform plus a third event for status-update failure, and the platform is repeated in `label`. Every conversion rate now needs a union, and funnels drop the failures.
findings.fix: Move to one outcome event per flow (for example wallet_created and wallet_backup_completed) with `status` and a bounded `failure_reason` enum, plus `cloud_platform` as a property. Map unknown errors to 'unknown' and log the message elsewhere. Don't rename in place. Add the new events, mark the old ones deprecated with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: wallet.ts:730-732 sends the raw `error.message` on wallet_create.failed. The registry shows the per-platform backup error events (useWalletCloudBackup.ts:131-138) and the separate status-update event (:152).

findings.title: A successful claim can also be reported as failed when the post-claim store refresh throws
findings.explanation: In both claim flows the post-claim balance refresh sits inside the same try as the claim, so its errors reach the catch block that sends the failed event. In claimRewards.ts the success event is sent at line 123. The user-assets and rewards-balance refreshes then run at lines 141-144. If one throws, the catch at line 151 sends rnbw_rewards.claim.failed for the same claim, so the claim is counted as both success and failure. In claimAirdrop.ts the refresh at line 90 runs before the success event at line 91. A refresh error therefore sends only the failed event, and the claim that really succeeded is never counted. Claim success rate and RNBW claimed are both distorted. The registry description for rnbw_airdrop.claim already notes this.
findings.fix: Send the success event straight after polling confirms the claim. Run the store refreshes in their own try/catch, or after the main try block, so they cannot reach the failure tracking. This changes the firing moment of rnbw_airdrop.claim, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line with the date.
findings.verifier_note: In claimRewards.ts the success event at 123 is followed by awaited refreshes at 141/144 inside the same try, with the catch at 151. In claimAirdrop.ts the awaited refresh at 90 comes before the success event at 91, with the catch at 116.

findings.title: Swap events attach whole asset and quote objects as properties
findings.explanation: `swapsSelectedAsset`, `swapsReceivedQuote` and `swapsChangedChainId` pass whole `ParsedSearchAsset` and `Quote` objects. These are large nested payloads that include icons, colours, network maps and balances, and `balance` is user wallet data. `swapsReceivedQuote` fires on every quote fetch, including error responses and the repeated refresh polling, because it runs before the error check. This inflates event size and volume and produces unqueryable nested properties. Compare `analyticsTrackQuoteFailed`, which sends only address, chainId and symbol and de-duplicates repeats. `claimablePanelOpened` sends per-asset address and amount arrays, which are also hard to break down.
findings.fix: Flatten to scalar properties such as `input_chain_id`, `input_symbol`, `output_symbol`, `quote_status` and `error_code`. De-duplicate `swapsReceivedQuote` as `analyticsTrackQuoteFailed` does. This is a breaking change for existing dashboards. Add the new flat properties first, dual-fire for one release, then deprecate the old shape.
findings.verifier_note: useSwapInputsController.ts:438-442 sends whole asset and quote objects before the error check at 444. swap-provider.tsx:1023 sends whole asset objects too.

findings.title: Browsing URLs and free-text names sent as event properties (favorites, trending dapps, prediction markets)
findings.explanation: `browserAddFavorite` sends the user-saved `url`, `name` and `image`. `browserTapFavorite` passes the whole favourited-site object as properties (`analytics.track(event, dapp)`), so any field later added to the type is sent without anyone deciding to. Favourite and visited URLs are user-chosen, can include arbitrary sites, and are attached to the wallet hash by the wrapper. The market name and slug are sent on every prediction order press.
findings.fix: Send an explicit allow-list of properties. For user-chosen sites send the hostname, or a flag for curated vs. custom dapp, not the full URL or image. Only send names for curated dapps.
findings.verifier_note: Homepage.tsx:226 calls `analytics.track(analytics.event.browserTapFavorite, dapp)` with the whole object. The registry shows browser.add_favorite sending url, name and image.

findings.title: Three events answer one question about how a wallet import starts, and 'read only wallet' fires for any address
items: Show wallet profile modal for ENS address
Show wallet profile modal for Unstoppable address
Show wallet profile modal for read only wallet
findings.explanation: The same action, starting an import or watch from a typed input, is split into one event per input format (ENS, Unstoppable, plain address, and a fourth for seed phrases). Rule 3 says this should be one event with an `input_kind` property. The 'read only wallet' event is also misnamed. It fires for any valid 0x address, including type='import', and not only watch. It fires inside the try block after the reverse ENS lookup, so a failed lookup (line 227) means it never fires, even though the flow continues to startImportProfile at line 239. The count of wallet additions that start from an address is therefore undercounted. The ENS and Unstoppable events fire only after resolution succeeds. A failed or abandoned resolution (line 153, 185) leaves no event, so there is no intent/outcome pair for drop-off.
findings.fix: Do not rename in place. Add one event, for example `wallet_import_started`, with `input_kind`, `type` and `status`. Mark the three old entries deprecated with `replaced_by`. Dual-fire for one release, and cut dashboards over by app version because old installs keep sending the old names. Move the read-only call out of the try block, or fire it in the catch path too.
findings.verifier_note: The rule-3 split, the firing on type 'import', and the missing intent event when ENS or Unstoppable resolution fails (lines 151-155, 183-187) all hold. One part is wrong: fetchReverseRecord (handlers.ts:839-848) never throws, so the read-only event is not undercounted and does not need moving out of the try (see F93).

findings.title: `positionsUSDValue` is set to the same amount as `positionsValue`, so one of the two is mislabelled
findings.explanation: When the user's currency isn't USD, the code adds `positionsUSDValue: position.totals.total.amount`. That is the same field already sent as `positionsValue` next to `positionsCurrency: nativeCurrency`. Either `positionsValue` is really USD and its currency label is wrong, or `positionsUSDValue` holds a non-USD number. Any sum or average of these properties is wrong for non-USD users. The `identify` call in `positionsStore.ts` also writes the profile property `positionsUSDValue` from the same `totals.total.amount` field. A currency conversion is needed on one of the two, or one of the properties should be dropped.
findings.fix: Confirm which currency `position.totals.total.amount` is in. If it is USD, send it as the USD property only and drop the native-currency label, or convert for `positionsValue`. If it is in the native currency, stop sending it as `positionsUSDValue`, or convert it. Since this changes the meaning of existing properties, introduce new property names and don't change the type or unit under the old names.
findings.verifier_note: PositionCard.tsx:81-83 sends `positionsUSDValue` with the same `position.totals.total.amount` as `positionsValue`, which is labelled with the native currency.

findings.title: Claimables user properties are built from runtime names
findings.explanation: identify() is called with one property per claimable type, named `claimable-${claimable.type}-USDValue`. The property set therefore depends on the data, and a new claimable type creates a new profile property that is not in the plan. The names also use a different style from the camelCase used elsewhere. Values are stored as strings, so they can't be summed or averaged.
findings.fix: Keep `claimablesAmount` and `claimablesUSDValue` as numbers. Drop the per-type properties, or limit them to a fixed list of types in the registry. Changing a type needs a new property name rather than a new type on the old name.
findings.verifier_note: claimables/query.ts:73-83 builds identify keys like `claimable-${claimable.type}-USDValue`, and the values are strings from add().

findings.title: Property type mixes number and string; events fire at unreliable moments
findings.explanation: `waitingTime` on `receivedWcConnection` is a number of seconds, but it becomes the string 'Error calculating waiting time.' when `receivedTimestamp` is missing. Analytics tools split or drop a property with mixed types, so averages go wrong. `learnArticleOpened` fires in the cleanup of a mount-only effect, so it fires when the screen closes, not when the article opens. Its `durationSeconds` is correct, but the event name says 'opened' and the count is of closes. Also, the deps array contains `url`, `key` and similar values, so any change to them fires the event again and resets nothing. The WalletConnect sheet fires two separate mount effects, `shownWalletconnectSessionRequest` and `receivedWcConnection`. These effectively double-count one sheet view.
findings.fix: Send `waitingTime` as a number only: omit it or use null when it can't be computed. If a type change is needed, add a new property name. Rename or document `learnArticleOpened` as a close or read event (SEMANTICS note in the changelog), or move it to fire on mount and add a separate `learnArticleClosed` with `durationSeconds`. Merge or document the two WalletConnect events.
findings.verifier_note: WalletConnectApprovalSheet.tsx:301 can send the string 'Error calculating waiting time.' for waitingTime. LearnWebViewScreen.tsx:33-45 sends from a cleanup whose effect has dependencies. The effect at 258-260 sends a second, separate event on mount.

findings.title: Rap completed fires on failure too, and callback(true) hides later-step failures
findings.explanation: executeENSRap sends 'Rap completed' unconditionally after the actions run. It sends it when the first action failed (callback(false, error)). It also sends it when later actions threw, because executeAction swallows those errors and the loop still ends with callback(true). A failed run therefore emits both 'Rap failed' and 'Rap completed'. Completed counts equal started counts, so a completion rate is always about 100% and the failure rate can't be read from it. 'Rap failed' also fires once per failing action, not once per rap.
findings.fix: Send the end event with a status of success, failed or partial, or send it only when every action succeeded. Make executeAction return per-action errors so the final status is true. Send one failure event per rap, or add the step index to each failure.
findings.verifier_note: actions.ts:687-700 swallows errors after the first action, the loop at 730-735 ignores failures and calls callback(true), and line 742 sends Rap completed unconditionally.

findings.title: predictions.place_order.failed can fire for an order that already matched and sent predictions.place_order
findings.explanation: executePolymarketBuyPosition and executePolymarketSellPosition start matched-order analytics inside the call. If the accepted response is already matched with hashes, predictions.place_order fires right then. The sheet then awaits waitForPositionSizeUpdate in the same try. If that throws, the catch sends predictions.place_order.failed for the same order. One order can therefore count as both placed and failed, and the later order_match.failed poll can add a third outcome. Place-order success rate and failure counts are inflated and no longer add up per order. The failure also cannot tell a rejected submission from a late position-size timeout.
findings.fix: Wrap only the order execution in the try that sends predictions.place_order.failed. Handle waitForPositionSizeUpdate separately: log it and show an alert, but send no failure event. You can also send a `stage` property so the two causes can be told apart.
findings.verifier_note: PolymarketNewPositionSheet.tsx:201 awaits waitForPositionSizeUpdate inside the same try whose catch (209) sends place_order.failed. executePolymarketOrder.ts:121 starts the matched-order tracking inside execute.

findings.title: swaps.quote_failed duplicates received_quote and its registry entry omits its real properties
findings.explanation: `swaps.received_quote` is already sent with the quote response, including a QuoteError, before `analyticsTrackQuoteFailed` runs. So the failure appears on a separate event (R004), and quote failures are counted in two places. The registry entry lists only the wrapper properties. The code sends `error_code`, `reason`, `inputAsset`, `outputAsset`, `inputAmount` and `outputAmount`, so none of what answers its question is documented. These properties are snake_case while the rest of the swaps events use camelCase.
findings.fix: Document the real properties in the registry. Longer term, put `status` and `failure_reason` on `swaps.received_quote` and reduce the payload to flat fields. Deprecate `swaps.quote_failed` with `replaced_by` and a dual-fire window. Don't remove it abruptly, because existing reports use it.
findings.verifier_note: swaps.received_quote fires for error quotes (useSwapInputsController.ts:438, before the check at 444). The registry entry for quote_failed lists only the wrapper properties.

findings.title: perps.closed_position fires before the close is confirmed, so one close can emit both a success and a failure event
findings.explanation: perps.closed_position is tracked right after closePosition resolves, before waitForTradeByOrderId, navigation and the trade-details step. Those later steps sit in the same try block. If waitForTradeByOrderId or anything after the track call throws, the catch branch also sends perps.close_position.failed. A single close then counts as both closed and failed. That inflates the failure rate and the closed-position totals and PnL sums, and a funnel on the pair will not add up. Failure is also split into two events, which goes against the one-outcome-event rule (status on one event).
findings.fix: Only the closePosition call should decide which event fires. Wrap the post-close steps (waitForTradeByOrderId, navigation) in their own try/catch so their errors don't reach the failure track. Moving the firing point changes what past data means. Add a changelog line starting 'SEMANTICS:' with the date and name the dashboards that use these events. If you split or rename events, deprecate the old entry with replaced_by and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: ClosePositionBottomSheet.tsx:150 sends closed_position, then waitForTradeByOrderId (163) and goBack (168) run in the same try, whose catch at 179 sends close_position.failed.

findings.title: Add-to-position cancel is tracked as perps.open_position.canceled, so it can't be told apart from opening a new position
findings.explanation: When createIsolatedMarginPosition returns nothing, the add-to-position sheet sends perps.open_position.canceled with market, side, leverage and perpsBalance. PerpsNavigatorFooter.tsx:237 sends the same event for the open-new-position flow. No property says which flow it came from, so the cancel count for opening a position mixes in add-to-position cancels. The add-to-position funnel (intent, then added or failed) has no matching cancelled outcome of its own.
findings.fix: Add a property such as `flow = open | add` to perps.open_position.canceled, which is an additive change. Alternatively, give the add-to-position sheet an outcome with `status = cancelled` on perps.added_to_position. Don't rename the existing event. If its meaning changes, go through deprecate + replaced_by with a dual-fire window, and add a SEMANTICS changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: PerpsAddToPositionSheet.tsx:213-219 sends perpsOpenPositionCanceled with no flow property.

findings.title: rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed can fire after a claim that succeeded, and cancelled signing counts as a failure
findings.explanation: The post-claim balance refresh at line 90 runs inside the same try block as the claim. If it throws, the catch at line 116 sends rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed even though ClaimAirdrop was accepted and polled to completion. The success event at line 91 never fires, so the claim is recorded as failed and the success rate is understated. Separately, prepareAirdropClaim sends the failed event at line 49 when signing throws. A user who cancels signing lands there too, so cancellation inflates the failure count. Rule 4 asks for `cancelled` as its own status that is not a failure.
findings.fix: Move the balance refresh after the success track, or wrap it in its own try/catch so it cannot send the failure event. Tell cancelled signing apart from failure, for example with a `status = cancelled` value or a `failure_reason`. Adding a value is additive, not breaking. Add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line, because the firing moment of both events changes.
findings.verifier_note: The refresh part is the same as F15 (claimAirdrop.ts:90/116). The new part holds: signMessage at line 40 throws into the catch at 49 with no cancel distinction.

findings.title: rnbw_rewards.claim does not say whether rewards went to the wallet or into staking
findings.explanation: submitRewardsClaim picks the endpoint from claimToDestination (default 'wallet'). The same rnbw_rewards.claim and rnbw_rewards.claim.failed events fire for a wallet claim and for a stake-rewards call. Neither payload includes claimToDestination or the endpoint. Claim counts and success rates mix two different actions and cannot be split. claimToDestination is already available in the function and is sent on rnbw_staking.stake.
findings.fix: Add an optional claimToDestination ('wallet' | 'staking') property to both events and to the typed payloads. Adding a property is additive, not breaking.
findings.verifier_note: claimRewards.ts:98 picks the endpoint from claimToDestination, and neither the success call at 123 nor the failed call at 151 sends it.

findings.title: Raw exception text is sent as the `error` property on two events
findings.explanation: The end-of-flow signing event sends `error?.message` straight from whatever the final step threw (signing, keychain, broadcast or RPC errors). wallet_initialization.failed sends `error.message` too. Exception messages are free text and can carry addresses, URLs or RPC payloads. They also have unbounded cardinality, so they can't be used for a breakdown. The design rules ask for failure reasons read from error enums or codes. The operation event also forwards the caller's free-form `metadata` object unchanged (line 56). I did not check the callers' metadata values.
findings.fix: Replace the message with a bounded `error_reason` enum (error name or code, such as WalletAlreadyExistsError, user_rejected or network). Truncate or drop the raw text. Whitelist the keys allowed in `metadata`. Renaming or retyping an existing property is a breaking change. Add the new property next to the old one for a release, mark the old one deprecated, and move reports over before removing it.
findings.verifier_note: performance.ts:74 sends `error?.message`, line 56 forwards the caller's `metadata`, and initializeWallet.ts:191 sends `error.message`.

findings.title: Error boundary events send the raw error object
findings.explanation: `onError` and `onReset` pass the caught `error` (typed `unknown`) and the full React `componentStack` as event properties. An error object can carry user-specific text such as addresses, API payloads or messages. The error object is serialised unpredictably by the PostHog client, often as `{}` or with a large stack. Sentry already receives the full error in the same boundary, so the analytics copy adds risk and little value.
findings.fix: Send `error_name` (the error class name) and `eventId`, which links to Sentry, and drop the message and stack. Leave the full detail to Sentry.
findings.verifier_note: ErrorBoundary.tsx:14-25 sends the raw `error` (typed unknown) and the full componentStack.

findings.title: `cashAmountEntered` fires on hold-to-add, before the wallet check, so it is an intent signal named like an input step
findings.explanation: `cashAmountEntered` is tracked inside `handleHoldToAdd`, once the user has held to confirm and before `checkWalletLink` runs. It is not tracked when the amount is typed. It fires again on every hold attempt, including ones that go on to a wallet-link sheet or a wallet-check failure. Analysts reading it as 'amount entered' will count confirmation attempts. The paired outcome is split across `cashWalletCheckFailed` and the buy-order action, which is not in this code, so I couldn't check it.
findings.fix: State in the registry description that the event is the hold-to-add confirmation. Longer term, rename it through deprecate + `replaced_by` (for example `cash_deposit_started`) and put its failure on the outcome event with `status` and `failure_reason`.
findings.verifier_note: The registry and the cited lines put cashAmountEntered in handleHoldToAdd, before checkWalletLink.

findings.title: Failed or errored signing is counted as a user rejection (`request.rejected`)
findings.explanation: When signing returns no result, or the wallet or keychain throws, the code calls `onCancel(response?.error)`. That sends `txRequestReject` with `requestType` and `isHardwareWallet`, and no reason or error. Hardware wallet failures and signing errors are therefore mixed with real user rejections. The rejection rate and the approve vs. reject funnel are skewed, and the send-transaction path has no failure event at all. The `txRequestApprove` call for transactions also sits after a try/catch that swallows errors, so it depends on `response?.result` being set.
findings.fix: Give the outcome a `status = approved | rejected | failed` and a `failure_reason`, or pass a `reason` to the reject event. Keep the existing event names (deprecate + `replaced_by` and dual-fire if they change).
findings.verifier_note: SignTransactionSheet.tsx:288-301: onCancel(error) always sends txRequestReject with no reason. Line 448 skips onCancel for hardware wallets, and line 523 calls onCancel when message signing returns no result.

findings.title: importedSeedPhrase fires for every import type, and tappedImportButton fires before validation
findings.explanation: `importedSeedPhrase` is tracked at the end of `handleImportSuccess` for every successful import. The `isValidAddress`, ENS and Unstoppable checks only decide whether to show the backup prompt. So watch-only and address imports are counted as seed phrase imports. `tappedImportButton` fires before the `!isSecretValid || !seedPhrase` early return, so taps that never start an import are counted. The intent event has no matching outcome with a status or failure_reason. Failed imports (the `setBusy(false)` and Alert branches) leave no event.
findings.fix: Add an `import_type` property (seed, private_key, address, ens, hardware) to the outcome event and a `status`/`failure_reason` for failed imports. Move the intent event after validation, or add a `valid` property. Both change what the existing events count. Record this with a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line, keep the old event name, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: useImportingWallet.ts:337 sends importedSeedPhrase for every successful import. Line 132 sends tappedImportButton before the validity check at 134.

findings.title: Amount-input events fire on every keystroke
findings.explanation: `onChangeNativeAmount` and `onChangeAssetAmount` run on each change of the text input and call `analytics.track` unconditionally. One send produces one event per digit typed. The rules say a text input should fire once, when it settles, and only if the value changed. These events add volume and no question anyone asks. The send outcome is already tracked by `sentTransaction`.
findings.fix: Remove the calls, or debounce them to fire once after the input settles. If you remove them, deprecate both events with `deprecated_reason` and remove the calls in the same PR.
findings.verifier_note: SendSheet.tsx:357 and :378 send on every change, with no debounce.

findings.title: WalletConnect failures are split across events, double-counted and use free-text reasons
findings.explanation: When namespaces are invalid, `rejectProposal` already tracks `wcNewSessionRejected`. The code then also tracks `wcRequestFailed` for the same failure, so one failure is counted twice. `wcRequestFailed` is used as a catch-all with a free-form `type` (`'session_request'`, `'read only wallet'`, a template literal for `invalid namespaces`, a template literal for `method not supported`). Its `reason` is a hard-coded sentence or a runtime `namespaces.error.message`. The result is unbounded values that split breakdowns. The `_failed` event shape also goes against the rule of one outcome event with `status` and `failure_reason`. `dappName` and `dappUrl` are sent on the other events with the same wallet context.
findings.fix: Use a closed enum for `failure_reason` (invalid_params, read_only_wallet, session_not_found, unsupported_method, invalid_namespaces) and keep the message out of the event. Decide whether the proposal path emits `wcNewSessionRejected` or `wcRequestFailed`, not both. The change alters existing events: keep the old names, add the new properties, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: onSessionProposal.ts:170-175: rejectProposal sends wcNewSessionRejected (62) and then wcRequestFailed is sent with the free-form `namespaces.error.message`.

findings.title: ENS names and token names are sent as event properties
findings.explanation: viewedEnsProfile sends the user's own ENS name as `ens`. That is a human-readable identifier tied to the person and their wallet. addFavoriteToken sends the token address, name and symbol, and the name and symbol come from remote metadata. The ENS name is the real privacy concern. The token fields are high-cardinality and add little a breakdown needs.
findings.fix: Replace `ens` with a boolean such as `has_ens`, or drop it. Keep the token address and chainId and drop name and symbol. These changes alter existing events, so use dual-fire or a registry changelog entry rather than silently dropping the property.
findings.verifier_note: useOnAvatarPress.ts:113 sends the ENS name as `ens`. The registry shows addFavoriteToken sending the token name and symbol.

findings.title: Claim failure event mixes user cancellations with real failures, and success/failure are two events
findings.explanation: The catch block computes `isUserCancelled` and logs it, but the analytics call never sends it. A user rejecting the signature therefore counts as `claimClaimableFailed`, which inflates the failure rate. The outcome is also split into a `Succeeded` event and a `Failed` event, so conversion rates need a union. It is money-adjacent, so the rules want one outcome event with `status = success | failed | cancelled` and a `failure_reason`.
findings.fix: Add `status` and `failure_reason` to the claim outcome, with `cancelled` when `isUserCancelled` is true. Treat it as a modification of an existing event: keep the old events, deprecate them with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: Airdrops/utils.ts:140-160 computes isUserCancelled but only logs it. The failure event always uses failureStep 'claim'.

findings.title: Claim failure is a separate event from claim success (rule 4), with inconsistent `claimableType`
findings.explanation: The claim flow sends `claimClaimableSucceeded` and `claimClaimableFailed` as two events, so a claim success rate needs a union of both. `claimableType` also has two sources in the transaction flow. Failures hard-code 'transaction', but success sends `claimable.actionType`. A breakdown by `claimableType` therefore splits success and failure into different buckets, and the failure rate per type is wrong. Failure reasons are the `failureStep` and `errorMessage` properties, which is the right data but on the wrong event.
findings.fix: Add a `claim_claimable_completed` outcome event with `status = success | failed`, `failure_step` and `error_message`, and use one `claimableType` source on both paths. Don't rename in place. Deprecate the two old events with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release because this is a money-adjacent event.
findings.verifier_note: TransactionClaimableContext.tsx: failures hard-code `claimableType: 'transaction'` (418, 441), while success sends `claimable.actionType` (470).

findings.title: Token launcher events send free text typed by the user
findings.explanation: getAnalyticsParams() returns name, symbol, description, logoUrl and the link URLs the user typed. Both the success and the failure event spread these into the event properties. The failure event also sends the raw error.message. The rules say never to send raw user text as event properties. On the failure path the token was never published, so this text is private at that point. Free text also makes the property values unbounded.
findings.fix: Send has_description, has_links, name_char_count and link_count in place of the text. Send an error code or enum as failure_reason in place of error.message. The creation event carries both success and failure. Per rule 4 it should be one outcome event with status and failure_reason. Changing the event shape is a breaking change, so go through deprecate + replaced_by with a dual-fire window.
findings.verifier_note: tokenLauncherStore.ts:379-381 and :438-440 spread analyticsParams and send `error.message`. The registry describes the payload as the whole form state, but I did not open getAnalyticsParams at :247-256.

findings.title: Wallet profile submit and cancel events record taps only and cannot be turned into a rate
findings.explanation: Submit fires at the start of handleSubmit, before onCloseModal saves the profile and before the keychain callback runs, so a failed save still counts. Cancel fires after goBack(). Nothing fires when the modal opens, so there is no denominator for abandonment. Neither call passes properties, so actionType (Create or edit) and isFromSettings are not recorded, even though both change the flow.
findings.fix: Add `action_type` and `entry_point` (settings or wallet switcher) as properties. Add an open/start event, or move the outcome event to the saved point with `status`. Do this as new events or extra properties, not by changing the old firing moment in place. If the moment does change, add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: WalletProfileState.js:61 sends Submit before onCloseModal and the keychain callback, line 54 sends Cancel after goBack, and neither call sends properties.

findings.title: Registry property lists don't match what the code sends
findings.explanation: initializeWallet passes `walletStatus` to finishMeasuring, and the event property type declares it. The registry has no walletStatus property. The registry's own question ('new, imported and existing wallets') can only be answered with that property. performance.report is sent with `reportName`, `segments` and `data` (the per-segment timings and extra params, such as the initial route). The registry lists none of them, so the per-segment breakdown that the question depends on is undocumented. The registry instead lists walletAddressHash and walletType as event properties of each event. Those are not passed by the calls. They come from the analytics default metadata, so they are context properties, not part of the event payload.
findings.fix: Add walletStatus (new | imported | existing, from getWalletStatus) to 'Performance Wallet Initialize Time'. Add reportName, segments and data to 'performance.report'. Note that the `segments` keys are the PerformanceReportSegments values and `data` is free-form. Keep walletAddressHash and walletType documented as default metadata. Additive change, not breaking.
findings.verifier_note: initializeWallet.ts:173-175 passes walletStatus, and trackMetric spreads it into the event (performance/tracking/index.ts:79-86). The registry doesn't list it.

findings.title: Rejected new WalletConnect session also fires for user rejections and double-counts with wc.failed_request
findings.explanation: The plan says the event fires only for invalid namespaces and not when the user dismisses the sheet. rejectProposal is also called when the person rejects (approved is false, reason USER_REJECTED), so the event covers both app refusals and user rejections. It carries no reason, so the two cannot be told apart. On the invalid-namespaces path the same refusal sends this event inside rejectProposal and then sends wc.failed_request, so one refusal is counted in two events. Rejection counts and failure counts are inflated and cannot be separated.
findings.fix: Pass the rejection reason (USER_REJECTED vs INVALID_SESSION_SETTLE_REQUEST) to rejectProposal and send it as a property on the rejected event. Drop the extra wc.failed_request on the invalid-namespaces path, or document that the two events overlap. Update the plan to say user rejections are included.
findings.verifier_note: onSessionProposal.ts:205 calls rejectProposal with USER_REJECTED, so the rejected event (62) also counts user rejections and carries no reason. On invalid namespaces it is double-counted with wcRequestFailed (170-175).

findings.title: performance.time_to_sign and performance.time_to_sign.operation are never sent when an async step rejects
findings.explanation: The plan says these events fire when a timed step returns, resolves or throws. In executeFn, a synchronous throw calls recordPerformance({ error }). An async step that rejects does not. The promise chain only calls recordPerformance in .then (success), and .catch just rethrows. A failed async step, such as a failed sign or broadcast, is therefore never recorded. If it was the last step, no time_to_sign is sent, and the elapsed-time counters are not reset. Timing data is biased toward successful flows. Counters can leak into the next flow unless startTimeToSignTracking resets them. The `error` property is also only ever set on the synchronous-throw path.
findings.fix: Call recordPerformance({ error: ensureError(e) }) inside the promise .catch before rethrowing. Replace the no-op .catch(e => { throw e; }).
findings.verifier_note: performance.ts:118-126: the promise `.catch` only rethrows and never calls recordPerformance, so a rejected async step sends no events and doesn't reset the counters.

findings.title: swaps.selected_asset fires on every setAsset call, even with no change, and twice on a flip
findings.explanation: analytics.track in setStoreAssets sits outside the didSelectedAssetChange check, so it fires when the person re-picks the same token and when asset is null. flipWithTracking calls setAsset and then sends swaps.flipped_assets, so one flip press sends both selected_asset and flipped_assets. Selected-asset counts are inflated and mix real selections with flips.
findings.fix: Move the track inside `if (didSelectedAssetChange)`. Skip it when didFlipAssets, or add a flag so flips don't send selected_asset.
findings.verifier_note: swap-provider.tsx:1004-1027: the track call sits outside `if (didSelectedAssetChange)`.

findings.title: token_list on the Send screen counts 'no_price' from the 24h change, not from the price
findings.explanation: The Send sheet increments no_price when `!asset.price?.relative_change_24h` is true. That field is the 24h percentage change. A token with a valid price and a 0% or missing change is counted as having no price. The registry describes no_price as a count of tokens with no price. So the send series is not comparable with the other screens. The same effect re-runs whenever sortedAssets changes, so one visit can send several snapshots and inflate counts per user.
findings.fix: Test the price itself (for example `typeof asset.price?.value !== 'number'`) and align it with the wallet and discover senders. Fire once per screen visit with a ref guard. This changes what no_price means for past data. Add a changelog line starting `SEMANTICS:` and note the change in the registry description.
findings.verifier_note: SendSheet.tsx:668 counts `!asset.price?.relative_change_24h` as no_price, and the effect at 663-671 re-runs whenever sortedAssets changes.

findings.title: swaps.submitted amounts are raw smallest-unit values, and errorMessage is always null
findings.explanation: inputAssetAmount and outputAssetAmount are Number(quote.sellAmount) and Number(quote.buyAmount), the raw amounts in each token's smallest unit. Summing or averaging them across tokens with different decimals gives meaningless totals. They can also exceed safe-integer precision for 18-decimal tokens. errorMessage is typed `undefined` for this event and sent as `errorMessage ?? null`, so it is always null and carries no information. The same params builder is shared with swaps.failed.
findings.fix: Add new properties for decimal-adjusted amounts (e.g. `input_amount_decimal`). Don't change the type or unit of the existing names, because analytics tools can't retype history. Stop sending errorMessage on swaps.submitted, or document it as always null. Rely on tradeAmountUSD for value reports.
findings.verifier_note: trackSwapEvent.ts:51/62 send `Number(quote.sellAmount/buyAmount)` as raw base-unit amounts. Line 49 sets errorMessage to null on submitted (typed undefined at :15).

findings.title: cash.buy_completed is silently skipped when a completed order lacks amounts or timestamps
findings.explanation: applyTerminalOrder only tracks when the order has cryptoAmount, fiatAmount, createdTime and completedTime. The order still goes to the success state and the purchase is still queued as a pending transaction. A completed order missing any field sends nothing. That undercounts this money outcome, with no failure event to show the gap. A buy_submitted vs buy_completed funnel would show a drop-off that isn't real.
findings.fix: Fire cash.buy_completed whenever status is Completed. Make the amount and timeToUsdcMs properties optional, or add a `status` property, rather than dropping the event. Because this changes the event's firing moment, add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line with the date. Ideally this money outcome would also be sent from the server.
findings.verifier_note: cashBuyOrderStore.ts:122 skips the completed event when any field is missing, while line 143 still sets success and has no else branch.

findings.title: wc.failed_request is a failure-only event with no outcome pair, and its failures lack dapp context
findings.explanation: The call sites send only type and reason. The question in the registry asks 'from which dapps', but dappName and dappUrl are not sent on any failure, although the data is available in the proposer metadata (onSessionProposal.ts:63-64) and in the session peer metadata. No call is made when the try/catch around approveSession fails, so that failure is invisible. The type union includes 'session_proposal' but nothing sends it. For invalid namespaces, reason is the free-form validator message (onSessionProposal.ts:175), so breakdowns by reason will split. The event has a start and a success (Approved new WalletConnect session, Showing signing request), so it is closer to a rule 4 failure event that is split from its outcomes. That is acceptable here because no single outcome event exists.
findings.fix: Add dappName and dappUrl, which are in scope, to the failure calls. Send a fixed enum for invalid-namespace reasons instead of the validator message. Track the approveSession catch branch. Do this additively, with no rename, so existing data stays comparable.
findings.verifier_note: The approveSession catch (onSessionProposal.ts:184-203) only alerts and logs. The invalid-namespaces reason (175) is free-form. The registry and type have no dapp fields on failure calls.

findings.title: Changed Global Notification Settings can never fire: the global topic list is empty
findings.explanation: `GlobalNotificationTopic` is `{}`, so `GlobalNotificationTopicType` has no values and the Settings screen has no global topic to toggle. The only call site is `toggleGlobalNotificationTopic`, after a successful publish, so the event is dead tracking. The `topic` property also has no possible values. Nothing is known about arriving data, because there is no snapshot.
findings.fix: If global topics are gone for good, mark the event `deprecated` with a `deprecated_reason` (no replacement) and remove the call in the same PR, per the removal rule. Keep the registry entry. If topics are coming back, keep the event and the registry draft, and note that it is dormant. Per-wallet topic toggles should go through a separate decision.
findings.verifier_note: constants.ts:11 defines `GlobalNotificationTopic = {}`, so there are no global topics.

findings.title: learn_article.opened fires when the screen closes, and can fire more than once
findings.explanation: The event is sent from the cleanup function of a useEffect, so it fires on unmount, not on open. The effect's dependencies are [category, displayType, key, routeName, url]. If any of them change while the screen is open, the cleanup runs and sends an extra event with a shortened duration. Counts of 'opened' are therefore really counts of closes plus any param changes, and an article that is opened and never closed (app killed) isn't counted.
findings.fix: Fire an opened event on mount (empty-deps effect) and send duration on a separate close or read event, or keep one event but read the params through refs with an empty dependency list so it fires once on unmount. Changing the firing moment is breaking for existing reports: add a new event and mark this one deprecated with replaced_by, dual-fire for one release, and add a SEMANTICS: changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: LearnWebViewScreen.tsx:33-45 sends the event from a cleanup with dependencies [category, displayType, key, routeName, url].

findings.title: `no_price` in the Discover token_list event counts the opposite of its name
findings.explanation: The loop increments `no_price` when `!isNaN(asset.price?.value)`. That condition is true when the asset HAS a price. A missing price gives `undefined`, `isNaN(undefined)` is true, and the counter is skipped. The swap-side hook counts `no_icon` correctly. In the Discover event, `no_price` holds the number of priced tokens, so any report on tokens without prices is inverted.
findings.fix: Change the check to `if (isNaN(asset.price?.value)) params.no_price += 1`. Because this changes what a property means, add a SEMANTICS changelog line with the date. Add a new property name if past `no_price` values must stay comparable, since an inverted history cannot be corrected in place.
findings.verifier_note: DiscoverSearch.tsx:115 uses `!isNaN(asset.price?.value)`, which is true when the price is a number, so the count is inverted.

findings.title: The Discover `Search Query` event fires on clearing the input, not when a search settles
findings.explanation: The event is sent from `handleClearInput` only when the user clears the input with more than one character. Searches that end by navigating away, selecting a result or dismissing the keyboard are never counted. The event also uses a different name style ('Search Query') from the rest of the plan. Taken as a count of searches, it undercounts and is biased.
findings.fix: Fire once when the query settles (debounced, and only if it changed) with `char_count` and `result_count`. Treat this as a firing-moment change, so add a SEMANTICS changelog line. Add a new event in the object_action convention and deprecate the old name with `replaced_by`.
findings.verifier_note: The registry entry and DiscoverSearchInput.tsx:133-134 show it fires only from handleClearInput when more than 1 character is typed.

findings.title: Trending dapp click is never tracked for the first card (`index &&` guard on a 0-based index)
findings.explanation: The call is wrapped in `index && analytics.track(...)`. `index` comes from `.map((dApp, index) => ...)`, so it starts at 0. The first trending dapp has `index = 0`, which is falsy, so its clicks are dropped. The top-ranked and probably most-clicked slot is missing from counts and from any breakdown by `index`. The guard was probably meant to skip a missing index, since the prop is optional.
findings.fix: Guard with `index !== undefined`. This changes the event's firing population, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line with the date. Position 0 will appear in charts from that release on.
findings.verifier_note: Homepage.tsx:333 uses an `index &&` guard, and line 160 passes the 0-based map index.

findings.title: Token list event fires on every asset change
findings.explanation: The effect depends on `sortedAssets`. It re-runs, and sends tokenList, whenever the asset array changes identity. That happens on refreshes, price updates and sorting, not only when the screen is shown. Counts of this event follow data churn, and the no_icon and no_price totals are repeated.
findings.fix: Fire once per screen focus, or once per wallet and address after loading finishes. Use a ref guard and keep `sortedAssets` out of the dependencies. This changes the firing moment, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: useWalletSectionsData.ts:117-126 depends on sortedAssets with no once-per-visit guard.

findings.title: addWalletFlowStarted is mislabeled and inconsistent between entry points
findings.explanation: Restoring from cloud backup sends `type: 'seed'`, the same value as restoring from a seed phrase, so the two paths cannot be told apart. The hardware-wallet path hard-codes `isFirstWallet: false` while the sheet receives `isFirstWallet` as a route param and passes it on to the navigator. Create-new fires both `addWalletFlowStarted` and `tappedCreateNewWallet`, and restore and watch fire both `addWalletFlowStarted` and a `tapped*` event, so each action is counted twice. The settings backup screen fires `addWalletFlowStarted` with `type: 'new'` and `isFirstWallet: false` but sends no `entry_point`, so it cannot be separated from the AddWalletSheet path.
findings.fix: Give cloud restore its own `type` value such as `cloud`. Pass `isFirstWallet` through on the hardware path. Add an `entry_point` property on `addWalletFlowStarted` and drop the redundant `tapped*` events through deprecate + `replaced_by`. Changing existing values splits breakdowns, so add the new value and note it as a SEMANTICS change in the changelog.
findings.verifier_note: AddWalletSheet.tsx:82-85 sends 'seed' for the cloud restore, 98-101 hard-codes isFirstWallet false while passing the real value at 107, and 45-49, 58-59 and 70-71 send two events per tap.

findings.title: wcRequestFailed fires on mount of an informational redirect sheet, not on a failure
findings.explanation: The 'no WalletConnect needed' sheet fires `wcRequestFailed` in a mount effect. No request was made. The user simply tried to use WalletConnect inside the dapp browser, which is a UX redirect. Counting it as a failure inflates WalletConnect failure counts for any other `type` or `reason` that uses the same event. `reason` is also a long free-text sentence rather than an enum.
findings.fix: Move this to a dedicated event or to `error_occurred` (client-side refusal, no request formed), and use an enum `failure_reason` such as `wc_in_dapp_browser`. Treat it as a modification: deprecate the old usage with a dual-fire window.
findings.verifier_note: The registry entry shows NoNeedWCSheet:36 sends wcRequestFailed on mount, with a free-text reason.

findings.title: Token launcher image-upload failure sends `url` and `isModerated`, which are always undefined
findings.explanation: `url` and `isModerated` are only assigned after the upload has succeeded. Every throw that reaches the catch happens before that, so both are undefined when the event is sent. The properties carry nothing, and moderation-related failure analysis isn't possible. The raw `error.message` is also sent as free text.
findings.fix: Drop `url` and `isModerated` from the failure event, or read them from the response before throwing. Replace the free-text message with a bounded `failure_reason` enum.
findings.verifier_note: useUploadToCloudinary.ts:14-33: url and isModerated are only assigned after a successful upload, so they are always undefined in the catch. error.message is sent as free text.

findings.title: Raw error messages are sent as event properties on token-launcher failures
findings.explanation: `error` is set to `error.message` from an arbitrary caught exception. The exception comes from the wallet and private-key loading path, in a catch block that wraps `loadPrivateKey` and token creation. The text is unbounded, so it can't be broken down, and it can leak sensitive internals. The failure reasons are also not a closed set.
findings.fix: Send a `failure_reason` enum such as `hardware_wallet_unsupported`, `private_key_null`, `not_authenticated` or `exception`. Keep the message in the logger only.
findings.verifier_note: TokenLauncherFooter.tsx:120 sends `error.message` from a catch that also wraps createToken (100).

findings.title: `rewards.viewed_sheet` fires on every focus, not once per open
findings.explanation: The call is inside `useFocusEffect`, so it runs again every time the sheet regains focus. That happens after returning from the explainer sheet or the profile sheet opened from the rewards cards. Sheet views are over-counted.
findings.fix: Fire once per mount with a `useEffect` and an empty dependency list, or guard it with a ref. Record the change with a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line, because past counts were inflated.
findings.verifier_note: RewardsSheet.tsx:43-47 tracks inside useFocusEffect.

findings.title: token_details.nft sends a nested `token` object that the registry does not document, including the NFT name and address
findings.explanation: The call passes `token: {isPoap, isParty, isENS, address, chainId, name, image_url}` alongside `available_data`, but the registry entry lists only available_data, eventSentAfterMs and the wallet context properties. The nested object makes breakdowns awkward. It also carries `name`, which for ENS and POAP assets can be user-chosen text. The 5s timer fires on mount and again via cleanup on early unmount. The call ignores the `cancelled` flag, so both cases look the same except for eventSentAfterMs.
findings.fix: Add `token` to the registry entry, or flatten it into scalar properties (`is_poap`, `is_ens`, `chain_id`). Drop `name` and `image_url` unless there is a stated question for them. Add a flag for the early-unmount case. Dual-fire any renamed property for one release.
findings.verifier_note: UniqueTokenExpandedState.tsx:389-393 sends a nested `token` object with name and image_url. useTimeout.ts:44-45 calls the callback on early unmount with `cancelled`, which is ignored.

findings.title: Completion event has no failure path, and the documented SDK-callback firing is not found in the code
findings.explanation: The only call sites for `f2cProviderFlowCompleted` are the two branches in the deeplink handler. The comment there says providers with SDK callbacks (e.g. Ratio) fire the same event from the SDK, but no such call was found in `src`. The type allows `fiat_amount`, `fiat_currency` and other properties that no call site sends. For non-`ramp` providers `success` is omitted (unknown), and it is never `false`. So the event counts returns to the app, not successful purchases. Deeplinks missing `provider` or `sessionId` are only logged, with no event. `provider` is cast to `FiatProviderName` without validation, so a malformed link can send an unknown value. Abandonment can only be measured as `flow_opened` with no matching `flow_completed`.
findings.fix: Report completion rates as a per-provider return rate, not as success. Check whether the Ratio SDK callback call exists elsewhere. If it doesn't, either add it or remove the unused optional properties from the type. Add this as an extension of the existing event (no new event). Validate `provider` against the enum before tracking. Describe `success` as 'true only for ramp' in the registry.
findings.verifier_note: A grep finds f2cProviderFlowCompleted only at deeplinks.ts:172/178, so there is no SDK-callback call. `success` is never false, there is no event when params are missing (151-157), and provider is cast without validation.

findings.title: BackupSheet shown is unreachable: BackupSheetSection is never rendered
findings.explanation: The only call sits in the useEffect of BackupSheetSection. Nothing in src imports or renders that component. A search for the name finds only its definition and two unrelated log strings. The event can never fire, so any report on how often people see the backup sheet reads zero. The registry profile lists the call as live.
findings.fix: If the sheet is still shown, send the event from the component that actually renders it (BackupSheet or BackupCloudStep), or render BackupSheetSection there. If the component is dead code, remove it and deprecate the event.
findings.verifier_note: A grep finds BackupSheetSection only in its own file, so nothing renders it.

findings.title: Updated Gas Price also fires when a screen picks the gas speed automatically
findings.explanation: The event is sent from the shared Redux action gasUpdateGasFeeOption, so every caller sends it, not only a person choosing a speed. SpeedUpAndCancelSheet calls updateGasFeeOption(URGENT) from an effect once gas params load, with the comment 'Always default to urgent'. Every speed-up or cancel sheet open therefore sends the event with no tap. GasSpeedButton also delays one call by 500 ms. The count of gas changes is inflated, and 'urgent' is over-represented. The event name is swaps-specific, but the action runs on every screen with gas.
findings.fix: Send the event from the places where the person picks a speed (GasSpeedButton and FeesPanelTabs handlers), or pass a source argument ('user' or 'default') and only track the user ones. Rename the event so it isn't swaps-specific.
findings.verifier_note: gas.ts:488 tracks inside the shared action, and SpeedUpAndCancelSheet.tsx:355-361 calls updateGasFeeOption(URGENT) from an effect with no tap.

findings.title: request.sheet.show can fire several times for one sheet
findings.explanation: The tracking call is inside a useEffect whose dependencies include transactionDetails?.payload?.params (an array reference), fetchMethodName (which changes with chainId), startPollingGasFees and stopPollingGasFees. Whenever any of them changes identity, the effect re-runs and sends the event again. The runAfterInteractions callback is also never cancelled in the cleanup. The count of sheets shown is then inflated, and so is the baseline for the approve/reject rate.
findings.fix: Send the event from a separate effect that fires once per sheet, for example guarded by a ref or with only the stable values it needs as dependencies. Keep the gas polling in the existing effect.
findings.verifier_note: The useTransactionSetup.ts:46-64 effect dependencies include params, source and callbacks, and runAfterInteractions is not cancelled.

findings.title: Completed ENS registration fires when the register tx is broadcast, not when the registration is done
findings.explanation: The event is sent right after executeRegisterWithConfig returns the broadcast transaction and the hash is saved. The transaction hasn't been mined yet, so a dropped, reverted or replaced transaction is still counted as a completed registration. The name says outcome, but the code only shows submission.
findings.fix: Send the completion event from the place that sees the register transaction confirmed (the transaction watcher), with a status. Or rename it and document it as 'register submitted'.
findings.verifier_note: actions.ts:404-424 tracks right after executeRegisterWithConfig returns the broadcast tx, before confirmation.

findings.title: claim_claimable.succeeded for airdrops is sent on submission, before on-chain confirmation
findings.explanation: The rainbowCoin airdrop flow sends succeeded right after provider.sendTransaction returns, before waitForTransaction. A transaction that later reverts or is dropped is still counted as a successful claim. The sponsored and transaction flows send it later, so the three claimableType values do not mean the same thing.
findings.fix: Add a status or stage property (submitted vs confirmed), or send the success event from the waitForTransaction result and add a failure when the receipt shows a revert.
findings.verifier_note: Airdrops/utils.ts:121 sends succeeded before waitForTransaction at 133.

findings.title: Viewed profile can fire several times for one sheet open
findings.explanation: The effect depends on params, ensName, profileAddress and accountAddress. ensName resolves after the sheet opens, and a new params object also re-runs the effect. The sheet can therefore send two or more events per open, with the first carrying an empty or unresolved name. The profile view count is inflated and the name property is unreliable.
findings.fix: Send once per open, for example guarded by a ref keyed on profileAddress. Or wait for the ENS name to resolve before sending. Drop params from the dependency list.
findings.verifier_note: ProfileSheet.tsx:66-74 has dependencies [params, ensName, profileAddress, accountAddress] and no guard.

findings.title: token_list from Discover also fires when the timeout is cancelled
findings.explanation: useTimeoutEffect runs the callback with {cancelled: true} from its cleanup when the effect re-runs or unmounts before the 3 seconds are up. This happens when `enabled` (not loading) changes or when the person leaves Discover. The Discover callback ignores that argument. The snapshot therefore fires at once on an early leave or a loading flip, and can fire again later. It is meant to fire once, 3 seconds after the list is stable.
findings.fix: Take the argument in the callback and return early when `cancelled` is true, e.g. `({ cancelled }) => { if (cancelled) return; ... }`.
findings.verifier_note: useTimeout.ts:40-46 calls the callback with `cancelled: true` on cleanup, and DiscoverSearch.tsx:103 ignores the argument.

findings.title: direct_sdk flags are a script artefact: `analytics` is the tracking wrapper
