findings.explanation: All 30 flagged lines call `analytics.track` or `analytics.identify` on the `Analytics` class exported from `@/analytics`. That class is the single adapter in the repository: it is the only place that imports `posthog-react-native` and calls `client.capture` and `client.identify`. It also adds the wallet hash, device metadata and AppsFlyer id, and queues events until init finishes. The scanner appears to match the method names `track` and `identify` without noticing that `analytics` is the wrapper. These are correct wrapper calls, not SDK bypasses. The one wrapper-bypass is inside the adapter itself, at `src/analytics/index.ts:169`. It sends the literal 'Application Updated' through `client.capture`, which is harmless but not typed through `event.ts`.
findings.fix: Teach the scanner that `analytics` from `@/analytics` is the wrapper and exclude src/analytics/index.ts from the direct_sdk check. No code change is needed at these call sites.
findings.verifier_note: analytics/index.ts:29-244: `analytics` is the wrapper and the only PostHog user. Line 169 is the one direct client.capture ('Application Updated').

findings.title: Legacy event and property names fail the naming pattern (R001, R007)
findings.explanation: The event names are set as string constants in event.ts. Some are Title case with spaces ('Error during iCloud Backup') and some are dotted ('mined_transaction.assets_resolved'), so they don't match the snake_case `object_action` pattern. The R007 hits on `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` come from one place. The analytics wrapper adds both to every event, and the wallet-context type declares them in camelCase. That explains the 70 property hits, which are a single convention mismatch and not 70 separate mistakes. These are consistent, deliberate names, not bugs. The fix is to accept the codebase's existing convention.
findings.fix: Don't rename in place. Renaming breaks every report on the old name. Either set `_conventions.yaml` to allow this legacy casing and camelCase wrapper properties, or record the exceptions. If a rename is wanted, add the new event, mark the old one deprecated with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: conventions.yaml event_pattern allows no dots or spaces, and index.ts:147-148 adds the camelCase walletAddressHash and walletType. This is a convention mismatch.

findings.title: Generic and inconsistently named events reduce readability
findings.explanation: `pressedButton` is a catch-all with free-text `buttonName` and `action`, so each new button creates a new value instead of an `entry_point`. The home-screen navigation events (`navigationSwap`, `navigationSend`, `navigationAddCash`, `navigationMyQrCode`) are separate events that all carry `category: 'home screen'`. By rule 3 they could be one action with an `entry_point`. Naming also mixes styles: 'Search Query', 'token_list', 'swaps.searched_for_token' and a camelCase `durationInMs`.
findings.fix: For new tracking, use object_action snake_case and an `entry_point` property. Do not rename existing events in place. Where consolidation is wanted, deprecate with `replaced_by` and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: Pressed Button carries free-text buttonName and action, and the home-screen navigation events are separate events with `category: 'home screen'` (see the registry).

findings.title: Trigger-order and add-to-position 'missing property' flags are scanner artefacts: the sibling success/failed calls are attributed to the wrong entry
findings.explanation: Every flagged call sends exactly the properties its own event is typed for. The scanner matched each call to the wrong registry entry, probably because the success and failed calls sit in one try/catch. Line 281 is the perps.trigger_order.failed call, not trigger_order_created, so it is flagged for triggerPrice, leverage and positionValue, which only the success event carries. Line 71 is the cancel.failed call, not trigger_order_canceled. At PerpsAddToPositionSheet.tsx:214 the call is perps.open_position.canceled and at :242 it is added_to_position.failed. Neither sends entryPrice, positionSize or positionValue. The reverse also happens: errorMessage is flagged on the failed entries at :268, :60, :214 and :228, which are success or canceled calls. The success calls (CreateTriggerOrderBottomSheet.tsx:268, TriggerOrdersSection.tsx:60, PerpsAddToPositionSheet.tsx:228) send every property their entries require. The payload types in event.ts (lines 1232-1286) match the calls. The registry's own descriptions note the scanner folded these calls together. Nothing here is a code bug, and no claim can be made about arriving data because there is no snapshot.
findings.fix: Fix the scanner's call-to-entry matching so each call is checked against the event name it passes, not its neighbours in the same block. Then drop the false property_missing findings. No tracking change is needed. In the registry, mark properties 'Not sent by this event' as required: false. This is already done on the failed entries, but not on added_to_position (errorMessage) or the trigger-order entries.
findings.verifier_note: The success and failed calls each send their own typed properties (registry entries agree). The scanner attributed neighbouring calls to the wrong event.

findings.title: Discover tab, section and carousel interactions double-fire: a product event plus a generic surface/placement interaction event
findings.explanation: A tab press, a carousel scroll settle and a card press each send a Discover-specific event and then a second generic event (`surfaceInteraction` or `placementInteraction`) with mostly the same properties (section id, section title, display). Analysts who count both will count each action twice. `discoverCarouselScrolled` is a scroll event, which the design rules say to skip unless someone has a question it answers; it is debounced, which helps.
findings.fix: Decide which of the two is the report event for each action, and document the other as an engagement feed for placements. Raise the question on `discoverCarouselScrolled` before removing it; if removed, deprecate it.
findings.verifier_note: DiscoverHeader.tsx:134-143 sends discoverTabPressed and then trackSurfaceInteraction for the same press.

findings.title: walletAddressHash / walletType are added to every event by the analytics wrapper, so the R007 hits are about one shared source
findings.explanation: No call passes these properties. `Analytics.track` merges `getDefaultMetadata()` into every capture and every identify (src/analytics/index.ts:147-148, 104 and 107). Drafting them as event properties on each event copies a global attribute onto each event entry. The camelCase names break the snake_case pattern, and they are undefined until `setWalletContext` runs. That is always the case for these two events: the probe fires at startup (App.tsx:177) and First App Open fires on first launch (App.tsx:198), before any wallet exists. Don't count on them for breakdowns of these events. Renaming them would break existing reports on every event.
findings.fix: Remove them from per-event property lists and document them once as global/super properties in `_properties.yaml`. If the camelCase names are ever changed, add new snake_case names (`wallet_address_hash`, `wallet_type`) next to the old ones, and dual-write for a window. Don't rename in place.
findings.verifier_note: index.ts:145-149 merges walletAddressHash and walletType into every capture and identify. _super_properties.yaml is empty and every entry repeats them.

findings.title: Registry drafts list properties these events never send
findings.explanation: The registry entries carry optional properties marked UNCONFIRMED that no call site sends. These are mode on phone_already_registered and phone_submit_failed, outcome and reason on phone_submitted, and reason and source on phone_verified. The event type map in event.ts declares only mode, reason or outcome, one per event. The extra entries look like the same call-site mix-up as in the first finding. They make the plan misleading, because an analyst would expect those breakdowns to exist.
findings.fix: Remove the UNCONFIRMED properties from the four entries. Keep only mode on phone_submitted and phone_verified, reason on phone_submit_failed and outcome on phone_already_registered. This is a registry-only edit: add a changelog line and make no code change.
findings.verifier_note: The phone entries list UNCONFIRMED properties (mode, outcome, reason, source) that the calls don't send, as the registry rows themselves show.

findings.title: WalletConnect property_missing results are calls matched to the wrong event, and the registry drafts carry stray properties
findings.explanation: onSessionProposal.ts has four calls, each for a different event. Line 38 sends wcNewPairing with dappName, dappUrl and connector. Line 62 sends wcNewSessionRejected with dappName and dappUrl. Line 158 sends wcNewSessionApproved with dappName and dappUrl. Line 175 sends wcRequestFailed with type and reason. The scanner compared each event against the other calls in the file: 'connector' missing at 62/158/175, 'dappName/dappUrl' missing at 175, 'type/reason' missing at 38/62. Each event's own call has the properties it is supposed to have. The draft registry also lists properties on events that don't send them. Examples are connector, reason and type on the approved, rejected and pairing events. The descriptions of those properties say 'Not sent by this event'. They are marked optional, so they cause no errors. They do make the plan misleading. wc.failed_request also declares connector, dappName and dappUrl, and no call site sends them. The wc.failed_request description says 'Seven call sites' but lists six, and grep finds six.
findings.fix: Fix the scanner's call-to-event matching. Remove the properties that an event does not send (connector, reason and type on pairing, approved and rejected; connector, dappName and dappUrl on wc.failed_request) from the registry. Correct the call-site count in the wc.failed_request description. These are registry edits only. No event is renamed, so no deprecation is needed.
findings.verifier_note: The four onSessionProposal calls (38/62/158/175) each send their own properties. The registry carries stray connector, reason and type rows, and the wc.failed_request description says "Seven call sites" but lists six.

findings.title: `identify` is called with chart settings on every change, alongside a duplicate event
findings.explanation: `ChartsTelemetry` calls `analytics.identify({ chartType })` and `analytics.track(chartTypeChanged, { chartType })` on each change, and does the same for `candleResolution`. Identify here uses the device id and writes the value to the profile, so every UI toggle becomes a profile write and an event. The events are also named in Title Case, unlike the dotted lower-case names elsewhere. This is a UI preference that a PM is unlikely to break a report down by.
findings.fix: Keep the user property if you segment by chart type, and drop the matching event, or the reverse, if nobody can name the question it answers (rule 1). If you do keep both, rename the events via deprecate + `replaced_by`.
findings.verifier_note: Chart.tsx:271-283 calls identify and track on each change.

findings.title: QR scan outcomes are four separate events
findings.explanation: The same action, a QR scan, is split by result type into four events. It should be one event with a property. The event names are also free text ('Scanned address QR code') and don't match the snake_case dotted style used by newer events such as `analytics_tracking.enabled`.
findings.fix: Add one `qr_code_scanned` event with `kind = address | profile | walletconnect | invalid`. Deprecate the four old events with `replaced_by` and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: The registry has four qrCodeScanned* events split by result type.

findings.title: property_missing findings are a script artefact: failure calls were matched against the success entry (and vice versa)
findings.explanation: The flagged lines are not calls of the entry they were checked against. claimAirdrop.ts:49 and :116 send rnbwAirdropClaimFailed ('rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed'), and claimRewards.ts:75 and :151 send rnbwRewardsClaimFailed. They were compared with the success entries, so claimId, claimedRnbw, decimals, pollAttempts and status look missing. The failure events correctly don't carry success-only fields. Going the other way, claimRewards.ts:123 is the success call (rnbwRewardsClaim) but was checked against the .failed entry, hence 'errorMessage missing'. The success call sends no errorMessage, as it should. The typed payloads in event.ts confirm the split. rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed has no registry entry at all, which probably caused the mix-up. The .failed registry entry also lists success-only properties (claimedRnbw, decimals, pollAttempts and others), with decimals and pollAttempts typed as string where they are numeric. These are stale draft values and should be removed.
findings.fix: Add a registry entry for rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed, with properties chainId, claimId?, status?, errorMessage, durationMs and platformRequestIds. Remove the success-only properties from rnbw_rewards.claim.failed. Fix the scanner's event-to-call matching so it compares each call to the entry for the event it sends. No change to the code's tracking calls is needed.
findings.verifier_note: The misattribution holds (claimAirdrop.ts:49/116 are failure calls, claimRewards.ts:123 is the success call), and the stale string-typed decimals and pollAttempts on rnbw_rewards.claim.failed are real. One part is wrong: rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed already has a registry entry.

findings.title: notification_permission.denied and .granted are missed when the permission request throws
findings.explanation: The request is tracked before the OS prompt. If requestNotificationPermission throws, neither granted nor denied fires. The try has no catch, so the error is not logged and the finally block still navigates to the wallet. These cases look like drop-off between requested and its result.
findings.fix: Add a catch branch that tracks the denied/error outcome, or log it, so every requested has a result.
findings.verifier_note: NotificationPermissionScreen.tsx:63-74 is try/finally with no catch, so a throw sends neither granted nor denied.

findings.title: An invalid OTP code is reported as `client_error`, and refused sign-ins have no outcome event
findings.explanation: In recovery, the server's `codeInvalid` verdict is sent as `cashPhoneVerifyFailed` with `reason: 'client_error'`. The server rejected it, so this mixes a user mistake in with real client errors in the `reason` breakdown. Separately, `cashSignInSubmitted` fires as the intent event. When the error is a cash-access refusal, none of succeeded, cancelled or failed is sent, so that attempt shows up as abandonment.
findings.fix: Use a distinct reason such as `code_invalid` for a rejected OTP. For refused sign-ins, either send a `failed` outcome with `failure_reason = access_refused`, or state in the event description that refusals are intentionally untracked.
findings.verifier_note: cashSignInService.ts:75-82: a cash-access refusal sends no outcome after cashSignInSubmitted. The registry confirms codeInvalid is sent as client_error.

findings.title: Token launcher abandonment is only tracked when the user confirms discarding
findings.explanation: `tokenLauncherAbandoned` is only sent in the discard-confirm branch. Exiting with no info entered returns early with no event. Abandonment is tracked only for one exit path, so drop-off is under-counted. `step_changed` is sent inside the store setter, so every `setStep` call anywhere fires it, including the REVIEW fallback after a failed creation, which looks like a step regression.
findings.fix: Send the abandonment event on every exit with a `had_entered_info` property. Add a `from_step` property to `step_changed` so a retry after a failure can be told apart from forward progress.
findings.verifier_note: TokenLauncherHeader.tsx:45-48 exits with no event when no info was entered. TokenLauncherFooter.tsx:112 calls setStep(REVIEW) after a failed or empty creation.

findings.title: dynamic_name findings come from the test file and from screen(routeName)
findings.explanation: In the test file, every flagged call passes analytics.event.<name> or a Routes constant to the wrapper. These are catalogued constants, not names built at runtime. These calls are unit-test assertions on the adapter and are not product tracking. In onNavigationStateChange.js, analytics.screen(routeName, ...) takes a route name from navigation state. The names come from the closed Routes set, but they are not literals, so the scanner cannot list them. The Routes set can still be listed from code, so these screen events are not unreadable tracking. The four duplicate hits on line 130 are one call.
findings.fix: Exclude *.test.ts from the scan. For screens, register the Routes set once as the source of screen names (the "Loaded A Screen" event) and mark the call as dynamic-but-enumerated.
findings.verifier_note: index.ts:91 shows analytics.screen takes a route constant. The test-file hits are assertions, not product tracking.

findings.title: The tracking map has the firing sites swapped for these two events
findings.explanation: `_map/error_boundary.yaml` lists both `onError` and `onReset` as fires_in for each event. In the code, `viewed` is sent only from `onError` and `reset` only from `onReset`. The path and trigger text are also wrong for `viewed`: its path ends at `onReset`. This makes the map misleading for any later impact analysis of this area, although the registry descriptions are correct.
findings.fix: Edit the map through a reviewed PR: `error_boundary.viewed` fires_in `ErrorBoundary.tsx#onError` only, and `error_boundary.reset` fires_in `ErrorBoundary.tsx#onReset` only. The registry entries are unaffected.
findings.verifier_note: map/error_boundary.yaml:7-9 and 24-26 list both onError and onReset for each event, and the viewed path ends at onReset (38). ErrorBoundary.tsx:13-26 sends reset only from onReset and viewed only from onError.

findings.title: Both performance events are sent only in production builds
findings.explanation: PerformanceTracker.analyticsTrackingEnabled is initialised from IS_PROD, and trackMetric only calls analytics.track when it is true. Dev and test builds drop the event, and the debug console log is off by default. Because of this, a missing event in a non-production environment is expected behaviour and not a dead path. Without a data snapshot, nothing can be said about whether production data arrives.
findings.fix: No code change. State the IS_PROD gating in the registry, as the descriptions already do, and verify arrival in production data once a snapshot exists.
findings.verifier_note: performance/tracking/index.ts:48 sets `analyticsTrackingEnabled = IS_PROD`, and line 85 gates the send on it.

findings.title: perps.trigger_order_cancel.failed leaves out properties that the plan lists
findings.explanation: The plan gives the failed event the same properties as the success event: leverage, positionValue and triggerPrice. The failed call sends only market, side, triggerOrderType, perpsBalance and errorMessage. All the missing values are available in the handler, because the position is loaded and the order has a trigger price. Failures can't be broken down by leverage, position size or trigger price the way successes can.
findings.fix: Add triggerPrice: Number(order.triggerPrice), leverage: position.leverage and positionValue: Number(position.value) to the failed call.
findings.verifier_note: TriggerOrdersSection.tsx:71-77 omits triggerPrice, leverage and positionValue, although all three are in scope (as at 60-68).

findings.title: swaps.failed sends the raw execution error text
findings.explanation: errorMessage is the free-text error returned by the swap rap. It is forwarded unchanged as a property, and the 'handled' sentinel is mixed in with real messages. Error strings from providers or RPC nodes can include addresses, amounts or request details. The type signature says string, but trackSwapEvent applies `errorMessage ?? null`.
findings.fix: Map the error to an enum `failure_reason` (for example handled, insufficient_sponsor_balance, unknown) and truncate or drop the raw text. This is a property change on an existing event. Add a new property name and dual-send it for one release. Don't retype errorMessage in place.
findings.verifier_note: swap-provider.tsx:342-347 forwards the raw errorMessage, and the 'handled' sentinel is mixed in with real messages.

findings.title: EthCard fires card.pressed only when the ETH asset has a native value, so some taps go untracked
findings.explanation: handleAssetPress returns early when ethAsset.native is null. That happens before both the navigation and the analytics.track call, so taps in that state aren't counted. Taps on the ETH card are therefore counted only after the asset price data has loaded. The same pattern means buy_button.pressed does not fire when the wallet is damaged, because the handler opens the error sheet and returns first. The registry descriptions already document both cases. Treat card.pressed as taps that did something, not as raw taps, when reading it.
findings.fix: No code change is needed if 'taps that led somewhere' is the intended meaning. Keep that wording in the description and the question. If raw taps matter, move the track call before the guard. That would change the firing moment and needs a SEMANTICS: changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: Both the registry entry and the cited lines show early returns before track: in EthCard when native is null, and when the wallet is damaged.

findings.title: cash.phone_submitted description is incomplete: its call sites are in three files and the first is shared
findings.explanation: The description lists three call sites, which matches the code. They are in different files than a reader would assume. The main one is advanceToChallenge in useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts, which signup, resume and recovery from the phone step all go through (the existing-account recovery choice reaches it via chooseRecovery). The `recovery` mode call is in verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts, and the `resume` mode call is in useSubmitReviewFlow.ts. The scanner's references only point at the shared file, which is probably why it matched the wrong calls.
findings.fix: Add the verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts and useSubmitReviewFlow.ts references to the registry entry, so scanning and drift checks see all three call sites.
findings.verifier_note: The registry lists the three call sites, but the code refs only point at useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts.

findings.title: Client-side 'Invalid amount' refusal is counted as a server failure on perps.added_to_position.failed
findings.explanation: The sheet throws RainbowError('Invalid amount') when the amount is 0 or less. The catch branch then sends perps.added_to_position.failed with the error message, although no request was ever formed. This inflates the failure rate of the exchange call with user input errors. Rule 4 sends refusals like this to error_occurred.
findings.fix: Check the amount before the try block and send the refusal as error_occurred with feature, action and error_reason, or keep it here and add a failure_reason value that separates 'invalid_amount' from exchange errors. Changing what the failed event counts is a firing-moment change, so add a SEMANTICS changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: PerpsAddToPositionSheet.tsx:201-203 throws 'Invalid amount' into the catch at 239-248, which sends added_to_position.failed.

findings.title: Redeem failure loses the relayer transaction details when waiting for the relayer throws
findings.explanation: `tx` is only assigned when waitForRelayerTransaction returns, at line 44. If the wait throws after the transaction was submitted, the catch at line 51 passes `tx` as undefined. The failure event then has no transactionHash, transactionId or transactionState at line 89. That is the case where the state would be most useful for diagnosis.
findings.fix: Capture the relayer response from submitTradingWalletTransaction before waiting. On failure, send its transaction id and state as optional properties. This is additive.
findings.verifier_note: redeemPosition.ts:40-51: `tx` is only set after waitForRelayerTransaction, so the failure event at 89-91 has no tx details when the wait throws.

findings.title: watch_wallet fires before the import, on an intent-only moment, and the `addressOrEnsName` value is inconsistent
findings.explanation: The event fires before startImportProfile, so it records intent with no matching outcome event. Failures or cancellation of the profile sheet are not measurable. For raw addresses, `addressOrEnsName` is the reverse-ENS result, which can be empty or null, or the address itself if the lookup threw. So the property mixes name, address and empty values, which makes breakdowns by entry type unreliable.
findings.fix: Add an `input_kind` property (ens | unstoppable | address | derived) to this event. Track the outcome through the existing import success path, with `status`. Both are additive, so no breaking change.
findings.verifier_note: useImportingWallet.ts:232-239 sends watch_wallet before startImportProfile, and `ens` defaults to the input (211) or '' from the reverse lookup.

findings.title: Registry entry doesn't match what the call sends or how it behaves
items: Show wallet profile modal for read only wallet
findings.explanation: The entry lists `address`, `addressOrEnsName` and `type`, which this call never sends. They belong to watchWallet and the imported-wallet event. The `ens` description says it equals the input address when no name exists. In fact fetchReverseRecord swallows every error and returns '' when there is no reverse record, so `ens` is an empty string in that case. The note 'not fired if the lookup throws' also doesn't hold. fetchReverseRecord never throws, so the catch around it is effectively dead and the event fires for every valid 0x address. The inner `ens !== input` check is therefore always true when `ens` is non-empty. The name says read-only, but the event fires for any plain address, including type 'import'.
findings.fix: Edit the registry entry. Keep only `ens` and `input` (plus the auto-added wallet context properties). Document `ens` as empty when no reverse record exists. State that the event fires for every valid plain address, whatever `type` is. Don't rename the event in place. If a clearer name is wanted, add a new event, deprecate this one with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.
findings.verifier_note: handlers.ts:839-848: fetchReverseRecord swallows every error and returns '', so the catch is dead, the event fires for every valid address, and `ens` is empty when there is no reverse record.

findings.title: Temporary debug probe event still ships on every launch
findings.explanation: The code comment says to remove the paired probe event after FEPLAT-67 wraps up. It fires on every app start, and it duplicates the installSource user property as an event. If the investigation is closed, this is noise with no question behind it.
findings.fix: If FEPLAT-67 is done, remove the call and mark the event deprecated with a `deprecated_reason`. Keep the entry, per the removal rules.
findings.verifier_note: The comment at redux/settings.ts:119-121 says to remove the probe after FEPLAT-67, and it fires on startup and settings load.

findings.title: Generic `cardPressed` event used for ENS cards, with the card identity in a free-text property
findings.explanation: ENSCreateProfileCard and ENSSearchCard send the same `cardPressed` event and tell themselves apart only by a hard-coded `cardName` string. `routeName` and `cardType` are also sent. That fits rule 3 (one event, a property), so it is not a problem in itself. But the values are free-text literals in the components, so a rename of a card splits the breakdown.
findings.fix: Define `cardName` as a typed enum in `@/analytics/event` and list the values in the registry. No event change.
findings.verifier_note: The registry shows cardName as hard-coded literals per component (card.pressed).

findings.title: Performance metrics use event names chosen at runtime
findings.explanation: trackMetric passes whatever `metric` it receives straight to analytics.track. The scanner cannot see the event names at that call site, so they are not in the plan. This is how dynamic names enter the project. The send is also gated by the `analyticsTrackingEnabled` flag, so whether these events arrive depends on a runtime setting.
findings.fix: List every PerformanceEvent value in the registry, or document this file as an adapter. Consider one `performance_metric` event with a `metric` property.
findings.verifier_note: performance/tracking/index.ts:78-86 passes the `metric` name through, gated by analyticsTrackingEnabled.

findings.title: Token launcher share event fires after the share sheet closes, whether or not anything was shared, and carries the deeplink URL
findings.explanation: The event is sent after `await Share.share(...)` resolves. That happens on dismiss as well as on a real share, so it counts completed share-sheet sessions and not presses. The full URL is attached on every event, which is a high-cardinality value. `address` is already sent, so the URL adds nothing.
findings.fix: Fire on press, before `Share.share`, or read the result's `action` and send `status = shared | dismissed`. Remove `url`. If the firing moment changes, add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line.
findings.verifier_note: TokenLauncherFooter.tsx:203-212 tracks after `await Share.share` with no result check and sends `url`.

findings.title: Leaderboard press sends the user's ENS name as an event property
findings.explanation: `ens` is another person's public name, but it is identity-like data. It is high-cardinality and can't be broken down. The event carries no `rank` property, which is what someone would break the press count by.
findings.fix: Remove `ens` and send `has_ens` and `rank` instead. The change alters the property set, so go through the modify path in `impact-analysis.md`.
findings.verifier_note: The registry shows the leaderboard press sends `ens` and no rank.

findings.title: qr_code.viewed fires on the tap, not when the QR code is shown
findings.explanation: The event is sent in the tap handler, just before navigate(Routes.RECEIVE_MODAL). The name says "viewed", but the code only records an attempt to open the modal. The tap and the modal opening happen together, so the count is close to real views today. If the navigation is blocked or changed later, the count will drift from real views. The same tap is the only way to fire it. Copying the address does not fire it.
findings.fix: Either treat it as a tap and rename it to something like qr_code.pressed. Or send it from the receive modal when it mounts, so it counts real views.
findings.verifier_note: Per the registry and the cited lines, the event is tracked in the tap handler before navigate(RECEIVE_MODAL).

findings.title: app_icon_unlock_sheet.cta_pressed is sent after the navigation and a 500 ms wait, not on the press
findings.explanation: The handler calls goBack and navigate, then waits 500 ms, navigates again, and only then tracks. The name and plan describe a press, so if the second navigation throws or the app is backgrounded during the delay, the tap is never counted. Presses are undercounted and the timing is shifted by about half a second.
findings.fix: Move the analytics.track call to the top of navigateToAppIconSettings, before goBack.
findings.verifier_note: AppIconUnlockSheet.tsx:34-39 does goBack, navigate, `await delay(500)` and navigate before tracking.

findings.title: Backup Complete fires for single-wallet backups too, not only 'all wallets'
findings.explanation: The plan says it fires from the onSuccess of backupAllWalletsToCloud. The same onSuccess is also passed to walletCloudBackup when a walletId is set, and that hook calls it after setWalletBackedUp. So the event covers both branches, with no property to tell them apart. The failure side is split: backupError for all wallets, errorDuringICloudBackup or errorDuringGoogleDriveBackup for one wallet. A completed-versus-error rate for all-wallet backups is therefore wrong.
findings.fix: Add a property such as scope (all | single) to Backup Complete, or update the plan to say it covers both branches. Use one failure event for both.
findings.verifier_note: useCreateBackup.ts:119-125 passes the same onSuccess (which sends backupComplete at 65) to walletCloudBackup, which calls it at useWalletCloudBackup.ts:146.

findings.title: Set App Icon is sent before the icon change is applied, on every tap
findings.explanation: onSelectIcon sends the event first and then calls settingsChangeAppIcon. That call awaits the OS icon change and logs an error in its catch, so the change can fail. The event is also sent when the person taps the icon that is already selected. Counts of Set App Icon therefore include failed changes and no-op taps. They are attempts, not icons actually set.
findings.fix: Skip the event when icon equals the current appIcon. If the question is which icon people end up with, send it after changeIcon resolves in settingsChangeAppIcon. Otherwise keep it as an intent event and add a matching outcome.
findings.verifier_note: AppIconSettingsSection.tsx:32-33 tracks before settingsChangeAppIcon, with no same-icon check, and that call can fail in its own catch (redux/settings.ts:173).

findings.title: Edited ENS records can fire several times per rap with no step in the payload
findings.explanation: Four case branches send the same event. A rap with several record steps (for example set text, then set address) sends it once per step. Nothing in the payload says which step it was, so the event count is not the count of edit actions and the steps can't be separated.
findings.fix: Send it once per rap after the record steps, or add a step type property (text, contenthash, address, multicall) and count distinct raps.
findings.verifier_note: actions.ts:400, 434, 440 and 446 each send ensEditedRecords with only `category`.

findings.title: perps.trade_details.share_pressed fires only after the share dialog resolves
findings.explanation: The name and intent say the Share button was pressed, but the call sits after await RNShare.open. A press where the image capture returns nothing, or where the share throws, sends nothing. Cancelled shares are sent with shared=false. The number of presses is therefore undercounted, and the name implies a different moment than the code has.
findings.fix: Send the press event at the top of handleShare, and report the result (shared, success) on a separate event or on a property of an outcome event.
findings.verifier_note: PerpsTradeDetailsSheet.tsx:61-73 returns early when there is no image, and the track call comes after `await RNShare.open`.

findings.title: Viewed ENS profile sends a hardcoded 'from' value
findings.explanation: onAvatarViewProfile always sends from = 'Transaction list'. The hook is used by AvatarCircle, which is reachable from several screens (wallet, profile sheets and others). Any 'from' breakdown will label every view as the transaction list, whatever screen the tap came from.
findings.fix: Pass the real source screen or entry point into the hook and send it as 'from'. Alternatively, remove the property if it can't be filled correctly.
findings.verifier_note: useOnAvatarPress.ts:111-115 hard-codes `from: 'Transaction list'`.

findings.title: Wallet init timer is never cleared on early-return paths, and concurrent runs share one timer key
findings.explanation: The timer is keyed only by the event name, and `Timer.start` overwrites any existing entry. The `shouldCancel()` returns and the nil-address return leave the timer running. They don't call `clearMeasure`. Only the throw path clears it. If two initializeWallet runs overlap (a switch while one is still running, or a cancelled run followed by a new one), the second `startMeasuring` resets the start time. The first run's `finishMeasuring` then consumes the second run's timer, and the second run finds no timer and sends nothing. The duration can be too short, and one run can go unreported. This is limited to rare overlap or cancel cases. The event does fire on success, as the plan says.
findings.fix: Clear the measure on every early return, for example with a `finally` that calls `clearMeasure` when the run did not finish. Or key the timer by a per-run id.
findings.verifier_note: timer.ts:6-11 keys the timer by name and overwrites it. The shouldCancel() returns (initializeWallet.ts:98, 112, 125, 141, 146, 161) and the nil-address return (156) never clear it.

findings.title: Tapped "Cancel" after editing wallet fires on any close with an empty name, not on a Cancel tap
findings.explanation: The event is sent from the else branch of 'if (name)' in onCloseModal, so it fires whenever the modal closes with an empty name, including after saving and after dismissing by swipe. updateAccountInfo has already run with an undefined label by then, so the label is cleared even though the event says the person cancelled. The count is closes-with-empty-name, not cancels.
findings.fix: Treat this as 'wallet edit closed without a name' (or send the cancel event only from a real Cancel action). Skip the label update when the name is empty.
findings.verifier_note: ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:257-268 runs updateAccountInfo with an undefined label, then sends tappedCancelEditingWallet whenever the name is empty.

findings.title: Tapped Edit fires on both entering and leaving edit mode with nothing to tell them apart
findings.explanation: onPressEditMode sends the event and then toggles editMode. Each tap is counted the same whether it starts or ends editing. A count of 'edit started' is inflated by the exits, and the event also fires when the tap only dismisses the hint tooltip.
findings.fix: Send the new mode as a property (for example is_editing = !editMode), or split the event into entered and exited.
findings.verifier_note: ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:410-415 tracks and then toggles editMode, with nothing to tell entering from leaving.

findings.title: debug.identify_probe (currency) can fire more than once per app session
findings.explanation: The currency probe sits inside settingsLoadState, which is reached through loadSettingsData. loadSettingsData runs once at startup and again in initializeWallet for every existing wallet that is not new or being imported. So the probe with probe='currency' fires at startup and again on each wallet initialization, such as switching wallets. The plan describes it as firing once in settingsLoadState. The event is temporary and diagnostic, so it only inflates probe counts and could confuse the delivery comparison it was built for.
findings.fix: When comparing delivery, count probe='currency' per session, not per event. Or send the probe only on the startup load. Remove the event once FEPLAT-67 is done.
findings.verifier_note: loadSettingsData.ts:12 dispatches settingsLoadState (which holds the probe at redux/settings.ts:121), and initializeWallet.ts:159-160 calls it for every existing wallet.

findings.title: performance.time_to_sign also fires when the person cancels or dismisses the dapp-request sheet
findings.explanation: In SignTransactionSheet the end-of-flow step is closeScreen, a SheetDismissal operation. onCancel calls it with canceled = true, and the confirm path calls it too. A cancelled request therefore sends a time_to_sign for a flow that never signed. A short cancel time pulls down the average time to sign for dapp requests. There is no property to tell cancelled, failed and signed flows apart.
findings.fix: Add an outcome property (signed, failed or cancelled) to time_to_sign, or mark the dismissal wrapper as end of flow only on the confirm path.
findings.verifier_note: SignTransactionSheet.tsx:301: onCancel calls closeScreen(true), the end-of-flow SheetDismissal, so cancelled requests also send time_to_sign with no outcome property.

undecided.title: Same `discoverPredictionOrderPressed` and `discoverSectionPressed` calls copy-pasted across layouts
undecided.explanation: The identical `discoverPredictionOrderPressed` payload is built inline in MarketCarousel, MarketGrid and MarketList. `discoverSectionPressed` is built in SectionLayout and again in PredictionEventsSection with different property sources (`section.destination` vs. `destination`, `section.display` vs. `surface.display`). The layouts have already drifted: card presses go through the `trackDiscoverCardPress` helper and order presses don't. A change in one place will silently desynchronise the properties.
undecided.fix: Move each into one helper next to `trackDiscoverCardPress`, so the properties are defined once. This has no event or property changes.
undecided.verifier_note: The copy-paste drift across MarketCarousel, MarketGrid, MarketList and SectionLayout wasn't checked file by file, and the finding asks for no tracking change. It needs an owner's call on refactoring.

undecided.title: Analytics toggle events are fired from inside a reducer
undecided.explanation: The reducer for the analytics toggle writes to storage, calls `analytics.enable()` / `disable()` and tracks events. Reducers are expected to be pure, and React may call them twice in development or strict mode. That would double the writes and events and make enable/disable state flip-flop. The disabled event is correctly sent before `disable()`. The enabled event is correctly sent after `enable()`, so ordering is fine.
undecided.fix: Keep the reducer to the boolean flip and run the side effects in the toggle handler or an effect.
undecided.verifier_note: PrivacySection.tsx:30-46 does put device.set, track and enable/disable inside the reducer. Whether React actually re-runs it in production builds (beyond StrictMode in dev) is runtime behaviour.

undecided.title: analytics_tracking.disabled / enabled are sent from inside a useReducer reducer
undecided.explanation: The track calls, analytics.enable()/disable() and device.set sit inside the reducer function. React expects reducers to be pure and can call them more than once (StrictMode, render-phase re-runs). Each extra run could send the event again or flip the doNotTrack flag twice. The 'disabled' event is also only sent if analytics was still active at that moment.
undecided.fix: Make the reducer pure (just toggle the boolean). Run the device.set, track and enable/disable calls in the Switch's onValueChange handler or in an effect.
undecided.verifier_note: This is the reducer side-effect question of F178. Whether it fires twice depends on runtime.

undecided.title: f2c.provider.flow_completed can fire again for the same launch link when the deeplink listener is set up again
undecided.explanation: The initial URL is replayed through `branch.openURL(initialUrl)` inside `setupDeeplinking`. That function is a `useCallback` over `handleRequestUrl`, `initialRoute` and `sendFailureToClient`, and the effect that calls it depends on it. If any of those values changes identity while the app is open, the effect cleans up and runs again. It then re-subscribes and replays the same initial URL through the listener. `handleDeeplink` has no de-duplication by sessionId, so a cold start from an `/f2c` link could count the flow as completed more than once. The code shows this path, but I could not confirm that those dependencies change in practice. If they do, completed flows are inflated and the match with `f2c.provider.flow_opened` drifts.
undecided.fix: Replay the initial URL only once, for example behind a ref flag. Alternatively, remember the sessionIds already tracked and skip a repeat in the f2c case before calling `analytics.track`.
undecided.verifier_note: Whether the DeeplinkHandler effect dependencies change while the app is open, and replay the initial URL, is runtime behaviour.

undecided.title: add_favorite_token: the exchange list calls toggleFavorite from inside a state updater, so it can send twice
undecided.explanation: The second route into this event (ExchangeAssetList, used by the discover/exchange lists) calls `toggleFavorite(address)` inside the `setLocalFavorite(prev => ...)` updater function. React expects updaters to be pure. It can run an updater twice, for example in StrictMode or dev builds, or when it replays updates. Each run calls `toggleFavorite`. Both runs see the token as not yet favorited, because the store is only written after the awaited metadata fetch. That sends `add_favorite_token` twice for one tap and inflates the count. The swap list (CoinRow) calls it from a plain callback, so it doesn't have this problem. The two calls the code scan found are the same line on one path, not two separate firings.
undecided.fix: Call `toggleFavorite(address)` from the press handler, outside the `setLocalFavorite` updater. Compute the new value from current state first, then call `setLocalFavorite`. Optionally guard `toggleFavorite` against a second call while the same token's fetch is in flight.
undecided.verifier_note: ExchangeAssetList.tsx:229-232 does call toggleFavorite inside the setState updater. A double send needs React to re-run the updater (StrictMode or a replay), which is runtime behaviour.

undecided.title: Sponsored claim 'unresolved status' failure check reads a stale claimStatus
undecided.explanation: The onSuccess callback tests claimStatus === 'claiming'. The claim handler sets 'claiming' and calls mutate in the same tick. With react-query 4.2.1 the mutation takes the options from the last render, where claimStatus was still 'ready'. This branch (failureStep 'unknown') probably never fires, so the plan's 'mutation resolves while still claiming' case is likely not measured. The same pattern is in the transaction flow. This is inferred from how the library works, not proven by a run.
undecided.fix: Track an unresolved result inside mutationFn, or have mutationFn return an explicit result and check that in onSuccess, instead of reading React state.
undecided.verifier_note: Whether onSuccess reads a stale claimStatus depends on react-query's options capture at runtime. It can't be shown from the code alone.

disproved.title: The wallet-sheet tap events have no registry entries of their own
disproved.explanation: ChangeWalletSheet fires seven events that the scanner credited to Pressed Button. These are separate events with their own names, defined in event.ts. The registry has only a Pressed Button entry for this area. Because the scanner's attribution is wrong, these events have no correct entry, and a drift check could misreport them. They also split one action across several near-duplicate events. 'Tapped Delete Wallet' and 'Tapped "Delete Wallet" (final confirm)' are an intent/confirm pair. The wallet_label property carries the user's wallet name, which is free text.
disproved.fix: Register each event under the name the code sends. Do not rename them in place. If you consolidate them into one wallet_action event with an action property, add the new event, deprecate the old ones with replaced_by, and dual-fire for one release. Stop sending the wallet name (wallet_label) as an event property. Send a has_custom_name boolean or a length instead.
disproved.verifier_note: screens.yaml already has entries for all seven events ('Tapped "Done"', '"Cancel" after editing wallet', '"Edit Wallet"', '"Notification Settings"', 'Tapped Delete Wallet', 'final confirm', 'Tapped Edit'), so they are not missing. The wallet_label point is F3.

disproved.title: identify() writes chartType and candleResolution to the profile, but the registry has no user properties
disproved.explanation: The same listener that fires each event also calls `analytics.identify({ chartType })` and `analytics.identify({ candleResolution })`. These write profile properties that the registry doesn't document (`user_properties` is empty). `identify` merges the default metadata, so `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` go onto the profile too (analytics/index.ts:85). Both properties are stale-prone: they are only written when the store value changes, and `set` semantics overwrite. The registry text mentions the identify call, but nothing tracks it as a user property, so drift checks won't catch it if the call dies.
disproved.fix: Add `chartType` and `candleResolution` to the registry as user properties. Record that they are written with `set` from the ChartsTelemetry listener, and list their enums. Then decide whether the wallet metadata belongs on the profile at all. Registering them is additive and not breaking.
disproved.verifier_note: user_properties.yaml already registers chartType and candleResolution (operation set, Chart.tsx:271/282), so the registry does have them. That the wrapper merges wallet metadata on identify (index.ts:85) is true but minor.

disproved.title: walletAddressHash and walletType are added to every event by analytics.track
disproved.explanation: The registry says these two properties are added to every event by analytics.track. That makes them super properties, not properties of one event. Registering them only on Pressed Button leaves the other events without them in the plan. The description also says walletType can be missing after initial wallet creation. Breakdowns by wallet type will therefore have an empty bucket for those events.
disproved.fix: Move walletAddressHash and walletType to a shared super-property section in the plan and document when they are empty. Identity (the wallet address hash) should be set at identify time. Keep the hashing as is and never send the raw address.
disproved.verifier_note: walletAddressHash and walletType are listed on every registry entry, not only on Pressed Button. Registering them as super properties is F132.

disproved.title: pair_hw_wallet_nav.entered effect returns the result of analytics.track as its cleanup
disproved.explanation: The effect is an arrow that returns the value of analytics.track directly. React treats a returned value as a cleanup function. If track returns anything other than undefined, React warns or errors on unmount. The effect has an empty dependency list, so it fires once on mount. That part is correct.
disproved.fix: Use a block body: useEffect(() => { analytics.track(analytics.event.pairHwWalletNavEntered, params); }, []).
disproved.verifier_note: Arrow-body useEffect returning `analytics.track(...)` is harmless: track returns void (index.ts:102-108), so React gets undefined as the cleanup.

duplicates.title: Search Query sends the raw text users typed into Discover search
duplicates.explanation: The clear-button handler passes the typed text as `query` next to `length`. Search text is free text and can hold wallet addresses, ENS names or personal strings. It goes to the analytics project as-is. The event type in event.ts also declares `query: string`, so the typed schema accepts it. `length` already answers the registry question (how long are cleared searches), so `query` adds risk and no benefit.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending `query`. Remove it from the event type at src/analytics/event.ts:1066 and keep `category` and `length`. This removes a property and renames nothing, so the event keeps its history. Mark `query` deprecated in the registry. Old data may already hold raw text, so consider purging it in the analytics tool.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F2: duplicate of F2. This is the same raw-query problem on Search Query.

duplicates.title: Raw token search text is sent as an event property
duplicates.explanation: The buy and sell token lists send what the user typed (`query`) to analytics. The rules say never to send search text. It's free text and can contain a pasted address or anything else. Only `char_count` and `result_count` are needed.
duplicates.fix: Replace `query` with `char_count` and `result_count`, keeping `type`. Do this as a modify with a SEMANTICS changelog line. `query` stops arriving, so deprecate that property and don't rename it in place.

duplicates.title: Wallet name typed by the user is sent as an event property
duplicates.explanation: The event sends the wallet label the person typed (wallet_label: name) as raw text. Wallet names are free text and often hold real names or other personal details. The design rules say never to send raw user text; send lengths or booleans instead. The event type in event.ts also requires wallet_label, so every send includes it.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending wallet_label. If the question is how many people rename a wallet, the event alone answers it. Add a new property such as label_char_count if you need more. Add it before removing the old one, and mark wallet_label deprecated in the registry. Don't rename or retype the property in place. Old values already in the analytics tool stay there, so decide whether they need deleting.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F3: duplicate of F3. It is the wallet_label problem at ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:264.

duplicates.title: Wallet name typed by the user is sent as a raw event property
duplicates.explanation: When the wallet profile modal closes with a non-empty name, the free text the person typed goes out as wallet_label. The event type declares it as a plain string, so nothing limits or hashes it. People often name wallets after themselves, an ENS name or a purpose, so this is raw user text, which the event rules list under 'never send'. The registry entry also lists action and buttonName, which this event does not send. Those belong to pressed_button.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending the name. Send label_char_count or a boolean such as label_changed instead. Since this changes an existing event, add the new property first and keep wallet_label for one release. Then mark wallet_label deprecated in the registry and remove the call. Remove action and buttonName from the entry.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F3: duplicate of F3. The action and buttonName rows on that entry are already marked optional and not sent.

duplicates.title: Raw scanned QR content is sent as an event property
duplicates.explanation: handleScanInvalid sends the full decoded QR payload as `qrCodeData`. This fires for anything the app can't recognise. In a wallet app that can be a seed phrase, a private key, a URL with tokens, or any other text the user scanned. This breaks the rule that raw user text is never sent. The event type declares `qrCodeData: string`.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending the payload. Send `char_count`, a coarse `qr_kind` bucket (url, hex, mnemonic-like, other) or a `reason`. Dropping the property changes an existing event, so keep the name and note the change in the registry changelog with a SEMANTICS line. Check the data already stored for this property and delete it if it holds secrets.

duplicates.title: Wallet group name (raw user text) is sent as an event property
duplicates.explanation: handleSubmit sends the trimmed text the person typed as `name`. It is free text and can hold personal data. It is sent before any validation, so empty names are sent too. The event name also suggests a name was chosen, but it fires on the submit tap, before onCloseModal and goBack.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending `name`. Send `char_count` (and `is_empty` if useful) instead. Changing the properties of a live event follows the impact-analysis protocol: add the new properties, keep the old event entry, and stop sending `name`. Add the planned new wallet-group event on success, with `status`, instead of treating this tap as a creation.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F7: duplicate of F7. Its submit-tap timing point also appears in the registry description.

duplicates.title: Separate cash.*_failed events instead of status + failure_reason on the outcome event (R004)
duplicates.explanation: The cash flow sends a dedicated failed event next to each success event. The failed events are declared in event.ts, for example cash.buy_failed (cashBuyOrderFailed), cash.kyc_failed and cash.sign_in_failed. The tests show they carry a reason, for example cash.kyc_failed { reason: 'rejected' }. Every conversion rate for these flows (buy, KYC, sign-in) needs a union of two events, and funnels that use only the success event drop the failures. The failure reasons are already collected, so the information exists.
duplicates.fix: Add status and failure_reason to the outcome event of each flow and dual-fire for one release (the old _failed event stays, marked deprecated with replaced_by and dual_fire_until). Move dashboards over, then stop sending the old event. This is a breaking change for any funnel built on the _failed events.

duplicates.title: Raw user-typed ENS names, Unstoppable domains and addresses are sent as event properties
items: Show wallet profile modal for ENS address
Show wallet profile modal for Unstoppable address
Show wallet profile modal for read only wallet
duplicates.explanation: `input` is the sanitized text the user typed or scanned: an ENS name, an Unstoppable domain, or a 0x address. The resolved `address` and the reverse-resolved `ens` are also sent raw. The app already adds `walletAddressHash` (an HMAC of the active wallet) to every event, which shows the intent to avoid raw wallet identifiers. These events send the raw identifier of the watched or imported wallet next to that hash. The rule is never to send raw user text, and a typed name links a person to a wallet. The input field is also unconstrained when the user pastes the wrong thing.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending `input` and the raw address or ens. Send an `input_kind` enum (ens | unstoppable | address) and, if needed, the same HMAC hash used for walletAddressHash. Dropping properties changes the event shape, so do it as a registry changelog entry with a `SEMANTICS:` line. Keep the event names.

duplicates.title: A 'handled' swap error fires swaps.failed and then swaps.submitted for the same attempt
duplicates.explanation: In getNonceAndPerformSwap, swaps.failed fires whenever errorMessage is set. The early return (alert and return) sits inside `if (errorMessage !== 'handled')`. When errorMessage is 'handled', execution continues past the failure block. It then adds the recent swap, clears gas settings, posts the rapCompleted notification, dismisses the sheet and fires swaps.submitted. One failed attempt is counted as both a failure and a submission. This inflates the submitted count, and any submitted-to-succeeded or failed-to-submitted ratio will be wrong. It also shows the user a success-like flow, including the rapCompleted notification, after a failure. No data snapshot was available, so how often 'handled' occurs is unknown.
duplicates.fix: Return after trackSwapEvent(swapsFailed) for the 'handled' case too, or move the swaps.submitted call into an else branch. This changes what swaps.submitted counts, so add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line with the date. Tell analysts that past submitted counts include handled failures. Confirm with the team that skipping the dismissal and notification for 'handled' is intended.

duplicates.title: Rap completed fires even when the rap failed, and the loop keeps running after a failed action
duplicates.explanation: executeAction catches every error, tracks Rap failed and returns baseNonce null. executeENSRap then runs Rap completed unconditionally, after both the success and failure branches of the callback. Any failed run therefore produces Rap failed followed by Rap completed, so completion counts include failures. In the follow-up loop (index ≥ 1) the return value of executeAction isn't checked. After one action fails, the remaining actions still run. Then callback(true) is called and nonce is advanced, so one rap can emit several Rap failed events and still report success. A completion rate built from Rap started and Rap completed will read near 100%. Rap failed counts failed actions, not failed raps.
duplicates.fix: Put the outcome on one event, as in rule 4. Add `status = success | failed` and `failure_reason` to Rap completed, and fire it only once per run with the true result. Stop the loop at the first failed action so the callback reports the real state. Because this changes the meaning of an existing event, add a changelog line starting `SEMANTICS:` and add a new property or event instead of changing it in place. If Rap failed is kept, consider deprecating it with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release.

duplicates.title: Rap completed fires even when the rap failed, so it can't measure completion
duplicates.explanation: In executeENSRap, ensRapCompleted is tracked unconditionally after the if/else. That includes the branch where the first action fails and callback(false, errorMessage) runs. It also fires when actions is empty. The event only means the function returned and carries no status. The question 'what share of started raps finish' reads as success, but failed raps are counted as completed. The registry description already says 'rap finished', not 'rap succeeded'.
duplicates.fix: Add status = success | failed and failure_reason to Rap completed. Source them from the baseNonce/errorMessage branch. This is additive. Don't rename the event or add a separate Rap failed event. Mark SEMANTICS in the changelog. Keep the existing 'finished' meaning for old data.

duplicates.title: Watched wallet addresses and typed ENS names go out in plain text
items: Show wallet profile modal for ENS address
duplicates.explanation: watch_wallet sends the full address and the typed ENS or Unstoppable name (`addressOrEnsName`) on every path. The ENS modal event sends the same address plus `input`, the user-entered name. The analytics client hashes the active wallet (`walletAddressHash`), so sending the watched wallet's address and name in plain text is inconsistent. It also links the user to the public wallets they follow. The registry already notes `input` is user-entered text.
duplicates.fix: Replace `address` with the same HMAC hash used for `walletAddressHash`. Replace the typed name with a bucket such as `input_kind = ens | unstoppable | address | seed`. Doing this under the same property names changes history, so add new properties and deprecate the old ones, with a short dual-fire window.

duplicates.title: `perpsClosedPosition` can fire and then `perpsClosePositionFailed` fires for the same close
duplicates.explanation: The success event is sent right after `closePosition` returns. `waitForTradeByOrderId`, `navigation.goBack` and the following code are still inside the same `try`. If any of them throws, the catch branch also sends `perpsClosePositionFailed` and shows an 'error submitting order' alert, even though the close was submitted and already counted as closed. The same close is counted as both a success and a failure. Also, the success event fires on the order response, not on a confirmed fill.
duplicates.fix: Narrow the `try` to `closePosition` only, or track the outcome in one place with `status`. Changing the firing moment is breaking: add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line and dual-fire.

duplicates.title: The raw caught `error` object is sent as an event property
duplicates.explanation: Both handlers pass `error`, typed `unknown`, straight into the event properties without converting it to a string or allowlisting fields. An Error object can carry a free-text message from any thrown code, and in a wallet app that text can include addresses, request data or user input. `componentStack` is also forwarded in full. It is long and not bucketed. The registry describes `error` as 'passed as received'. The shape serialized by the analytics client is unknown. Sentry already holds the full error, and `eventId` links to it.
duplicates.fix: Stop sending the raw error. Send `eventId` (the Sentry link) and a bounded `error_name` (the error class name). If a message is needed, send a truncated, scrubbed version. Treat the removal of `error` from the existing events as a change to the property list: update the registry and add a changelog line.

duplicates.title: perps.closed_position fires before the close is confirmed, so one close can also send perps.close_position.failed
duplicates.explanation: perps.closed_position is sent right after closePosition resolves, before waitForTradeByOrderId and navigation. Everything after it is inside the same try. If waitForTradeByOrderId or a later step throws, the catch also sends perps.close_position.failed for the same close, and an Alert tells the person it failed, even though the exchange already accepted the close. The close counts as both a success and a failure. The failure rate is inflated, and the success and failure counts can't be added up as separate closes.
duplicates.fix: Keep the try around the close request only and send the failed event there. Move the post-close work (waitForTradeByOrderId, navigation) into its own try that can't send perps.close_position.failed. Or add a stage property so the two cases are separable.

duplicates.title: perps.open_position.canceled also counts cancelled adds to an existing position
duplicates.explanation: The add-to-position sheet sends the new-position cancel event when createIsolatedMarginPosition returns nothing. The success and failure of the same flow use separate add events (perps.added_to_position and perps.added_to_position.failed). So cancelled adds inflate the cancel count for opening new positions. The opened/cancelled ratio for new positions is wrong, and adds have no cancel event of their own.
duplicates.fix: Send cancelled adds under an add-specific event, or put a status of cancelled on the outcome event. If one event is kept, add a property saying whether it was a new position or an add.

duplicates.title: Position and asset values are USD amounts but are labelled with the person's native currency
duplicates.explanation: The value fields (position.totals.total.amount and the asset value passed to openTokenSheet) are USD amounts. The position types and fixtures show display strings like '$1,500.25'. The calls send them as assetValue and positionsValue next to assetCurrency and positionsCurrency set to the native currency. For non-USD users the number is USD but the currency says EUR, for example. For those users the code also sends positionsUSDValue with the same unconverted amount, so the USD property is simply a copy of the value field. Totals by currency are wrong for those users.
duplicates.fix: Send the value as USD (positionsUSDValue, assetValueUSD) and drop the native-currency label. If a native-currency value is wanted, convert the USD amount with the exchange rate before sending it.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F19: duplicate of F19. Whether totals.total.amount is in USD or the native currency is still unresolved.

duplicates.title: Claim success event can be followed by a failure event for the same claim (rnbw_rewards.claim, rnbw_rewards.claim.failed)
duplicates.explanation: In submitRewardsClaim the success event is sent at line 123. The user-assets and rewards-balance refreshes at lines 141-144 are still inside the same try. If either refresh throws, the catch sends rnbw_rewards.claim.failed for a claim that already succeeded and was already counted. One claim then shows as both success and failure, which inflates the failure count and understates the success rate.
duplicates.fix: Move the store refreshes out of the try, or wrap them in their own try/catch so they can't reach the failure tracking. Do the same in submitAirdropClaim.

duplicates.title: token_launcher.token_created is sent before the launch has finished its follow-up work, so creation_failed can follow it
duplicates.explanation: token_created is sent right after launchToken returns, but the same try block then awaits publicClient.getTransaction and addNewTransaction. If either throws, the catch sends creation_failed for a launch already counted as created. The catch also returns nothing, so the footer treats the launch as empty and sets the REVIEW step. The same launch can therefore appear as both created and failed, which inflates failures and makes the created-to-failed split unreliable.
duplicates.fix: Wrap the post-launch work (getTransaction, addNewTransaction) in its own try/catch that logs without sending creation_failed. Or send token_created only once that work is done. Send a creation_failed only for errors from launchToken.

duplicates.title: swaps.submitted also fires after a 'handled' swap failure
duplicates.explanation: When the rap returns errorMessage 'handled', the error branch sends swaps.failed. It skips the alert and the early return, which only run for other errors. Execution then falls through to the dismiss-sheet code and sends swaps.submitted. One failed swap therefore counts as both failed and submitted. Submitted is overstated, the failed/submitted split no longer adds up, and the submit-to-succeeded conversion looks worse than it is.
duplicates.fix: Return after trackSwapEvent(swapsFailed) for every error, including 'handled'. Or send swaps.submitted only when errorMessage is falsy.

duplicates.title: A 'handled' swap error fires swaps.failed and then swaps.submitted for the same attempt
duplicates.explanation: When errorMessage is set, swaps.failed is tracked. If the message is exactly 'handled', the code skips the alert and the return, and carries on to the success path. That path schedules the sheet dismissal and fires swaps.submitted. One failed swap is therefore counted as both failed and submitted, which inflates the submitted count and any submitted→succeeded conversion rate. This is the same uncertainty the registry description flags.
duplicates.fix: Confirm with the team whether 'handled' should also dismiss the sheet. If not, return after the failed event for 'handled' too, or guard the submitted call with `if (!errorMessage)`. This changes the firing moment of swaps.submitted, so add a changelog line starting `SEMANTICS:` with the date. Don't rename the event.

duplicates.title: Amount properties on swaps.submitted are raw smallest-unit values
duplicates.explanation: `inputAssetAmount` and `outputAssetAmount` are `Number(quote.sellAmount)` and `Number(quote.buyAmount)`. These are raw base-unit amounts, so 18-decimal tokens give values around 1e18 and 6-decimal tokens give values around 1e6. They can't be summed or averaged across tokens, and large values lose precision when converted to Number. Only `tradeAmountUSD` is comparable across swaps.
duplicates.fix: Add new properties with decimal-adjusted amounts, for example `input_amount_decimal`. Don't change the type or meaning of the old names. Keep `tradeAmountUSD` as the cross-token measure.

duplicates.title: swaps.selected_asset fires on every setAsset call and sends whole asset objects
duplicates.explanation: The `analytics.track` call sits outside the `didSelectedAssetChange` check, so it fires even when the selection didn't change. It sends the full `asset` and `otherAsset` objects, which can be null. These are ParsedSearchAsset objects with prices, icons and network maps. That makes the payload large and unpredictable, and hard to break down by symbol or chain. The registry also lists many properties that belong to swaps.submitted (`degenMode`, `inputAsset*`, `tradeAmountUSD` and others). This call doesn't send them.
duplicates.fix: Move the call inside the `didSelectedAssetChange` block. Send flat fields instead of objects: `symbol`, `address`, `chainId` and the same three for the other side. Remove the cross-contaminated properties from the registry entry. Any change to the firing moment or properties is a SEMANTICS change with a changelog line.

duplicates.title: rnbw_rewards.claim cannot tell a wallet claim from a stake-rewards claim
duplicates.explanation: submitRewardsClaim picks the endpoint from claimToDestination: /rewards/ClaimRewards for 'wallet', /staking/StakeRewards otherwise. Both paths fire the same rnbwRewardsClaim event, and no property carries the destination. The claimedRnbw totals and the success rate mix two different actions. This undermines the registry question 'how much RNBW is claimed'.
duplicates.fix: Add an optional property such as claim_destination (wallet | stake) to rnbw_rewards.claim and rnbw_rewards.claim.failed. This is additive and not breaking. Add a changelog line. Do not split the event.

duplicates.title: Airdrop claim failures include user cancellations and send the raw exception text
duplicates.explanation: claimAirdrop works out isUserCancelled from the exception text but only logs it. The analytics call still sends claim_claimable.failed with failureStep 'claim' for a cancel or rejection. A person backing out of the signing prompt is counted as a failed claim, which inflates the failure rate for rainbowCoin. The same call sends the raw exception message as errorMessage. The sponsored and transaction flows send constants from the ErrorMessages enum, so errorMessage has mixed meanings (enum values vs free text) and can't be grouped cleanly. claimableId is also different here: uniqueId (airdropId) instead of claimable.type.
duplicates.fix: Add a status property (failed vs cancelled) on the claim outcome, or skip the event when isUserCancelled is true, so cancellations stop counting as failures. Map exception text to an ErrorMessages-style constant instead of sending the raw message. Use one definition of claimableId across the three flows. Because this changes what the event counts, give it a SEMANTICS: changelog line and a new property name where the meaning changes.

duplicates.title: Buy-order completion is silently not tracked when any amount or timestamp field is missing
duplicates.explanation: A completed order only sends `cashBuyOrderCompleted` if `cryptoAmount`, `fiatAmount`, `createdTime` and `completedTime` are all present. There is no else branch. The same completed order is still added to pending transactions and the UI moves to success. Any completed order missing one of those fields is therefore a purchase that never reaches analytics, and nothing flags it. The event also fires on the client, and only when the app is open to see the terminal state. The failure path (`cashBuyOrderFailed`) has no such guard, so completion and failure counts are not comparable.
duplicates.fix: Always send the completion event for a completed order. Make `cryptoAmount`, `fiatAmount` and `timeToUsdcMs` optional, or log a warning when they are absent. Prefer a server-side emit so completions are counted when no user is present. Any change to this money event goes through deprecate, `replaced_by` and a dual-fire window.

duplicates.title: wallet_create.failed sends the raw exception message as its failure reason
duplicates.explanation: Three paths send fixed codes (`wallet_or_address_missing`, `wallet_already_exists`, `wallet_already_exists_restoring`). The catch branch sends `error.message` unchanged. That covers keychain and derivation errors, and some messages are localized or may include dynamic text. The `error` property therefore has unbounded cardinality, which splits breakdowns. The free text could also carry sensitive detail. The same event has a mixed vocabulary of codes and messages.
duplicates.fix: Map caught errors to a short enum (for example `keychain_error`, `derivation_error`, `unknown`) and send that. Keep the raw message in the logger only. Changing the values of `error` is an enum change, so list it in the changelog. Failure also lives on a separate `.failed` event, which rule 4 says should be a `status` + `failure_reason` on one outcome event. Handle that in the same migration as the naming decision above.

duplicates.title: cash.buy_completed is silently skipped for a completed order missing a field, while the UI shows success
duplicates.explanation: applyTerminalOrder sends the event only if cryptoAmount, fiatAmount, createdTime and completedTime are all present. The ramp client parses these fields leniently, so they can be missing. The state still moves to success and the purchase transaction is still queued. Such an order reaches the person as a success, but no completed event is sent and no failure event is sent either. Completed-buy counts, volume and time-to-USDC are undercounted, and funnels from cash.buy_submitted show a drop that did not happen.
duplicates.fix: Always send cash.buy_completed when status is Completed, and send each property only when it is available (leave timeToUsdcMs unset if a timestamp is missing). This also avoids a silent gap between submitted and completed.

duplicates.title: Trending dapp click is never sent for the first tile, recents or the featured card
duplicates.explanation: The call is guarded by `index &&`. Index 0 is falsy, so the first trending dapp, usually the most clicked, is never counted. Recents cards and the featured card have no index prop at all, so they never send it either, although the plan describes it as covering trending and recents. Click counts per dapp are biased and the first slot is missing.
duplicates.fix: Guard with `index !== undefined`. Send recents as their own source value if they should be tracked, or leave them out. Add a property saying which list the card came from.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F53: duplicate of F53. Recents cards (Homepage.tsx:289) pass no index, so they never send it either.

duplicates.title: rnbw_airdrop.claim is skipped, and claim.failed sent, when the post-claim balance refresh throws
duplicates.explanation: submitAirdropClaim awaits the airdrop balance store refresh before sending rnbw_airdrop.claim. That call is inside the same try as the claim. If the refresh throws after the claim was accepted and polled to a non-failed status, the success event never fires and the catch sends rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed instead. The user's claim went through, so the claim count is too low and the failure count too high. The failed event also carries the real claimId and status, which makes a successful claim look like a failure.
duplicates.fix: Send rnbw_airdrop.claim right after pollForClaimStatus returns, before the balance and asset refreshes. Put the refreshes in their own try/catch that only logs.

duplicates.title: add_wallet_flow.started: cloud restore is reported as type 'seed', hardware wallet hard-codes isFirstWallet false
duplicates.explanation: onPressRestoreFromCloud sends the same type value ('seed') as the restore-from-seed option, so the two ways in can't be told apart in a breakdown by type. The hardware wallet option hard-codes isFirstWallet: false instead of using the sheet's isFirstWallet value, so first-wallet counts are wrong for that path. The event is also an intent only, with no outcome event, so no completion rate can be computed.
duplicates.fix: Give cloud restore its own type value (for example 'cloud'). Pass the real isFirstWallet in the hardware wallet call. Add an outcome event for wallet added.

duplicates.title: learn_article.opened is sent when the screen closes, not when the article opens
duplicates.explanation: The call sits in the cleanup function of a useEffect, so it runs on unmount. The name says the article was opened. Opens are counted only when the person leaves. An app kill or background while reading never sends it. The effect depends on category, displayType, key, routeName and url, so a change to any of them while the screen is open runs the cleanup and sends an extra event with a partial duration.
