duplicates.fix: Send an open event on mount (empty-deps effect or on view). Keep the duration in a separate event or property, such as learn_article.closed, sent from an unmount-only cleanup that reads params from refs.

duplicates.title: claim_claimable.failed counts user-cancelled transactions as failures
duplicates.explanation: In the airdrop flow the catch block works out isUserCancelled (denied, cancelled, rejected) and logs it. The analytics call does not send it and always uses failureStep 'claim'. A person who backs out of signing is counted as a failed claim, which inflates the failure rate. The design rules say cancelled is a separate status and not a failure.
duplicates.fix: Add a status or failure_reason property (success | failed | cancelled) and send cancelled when isUserCancelled is true. Apply the same split in the sponsored and transaction flows.

duplicates.title: token_list from Discover counts tokens that HAVE a price as no_price
duplicates.explanation: The Discover sender increments no_price when `!isNaN(asset.price?.value)`, which is true when the price is a number. The condition is inverted, so no_price reports priced tokens and reads near total_tokens. The wallet sender counts a token with no relative_change_24h, so no_price means something different on each screen. The swap sender doesn't send no_price at all. The plan lists no_price as a property of the event.
duplicates.fix: Use `isNaN(asset.price?.value)` (or a null check) in Discover. Use the same definition of 'no price' on every screen, and add no_price to the swap sender.

duplicates.title: All 29 `direct_sdk` findings are a script artefact: `@/analytics` is the wrapper, not the SDK
duplicates.explanation: Every flagged call goes through `analytics.track(...)` or `analytics.identify(...)` imported from `@/analytics`. That is the project's own typed wrapper, the `Analytics` class in `src/analytics/index.ts`. It is the only place that touches the `posthog-react-native` client, through `client.capture` and `client.identify`. The wrapper adds wallet metadata, the AppsFlyer id, a queue before init, and a doNotTrack and test gate. The scanner's profile appears to treat the wrapper's own method names as SDK calls, so these calls are the sanctioned path and not bypasses. The scanner profile should list `analytics.track`, `analytics.identify` and `analytics.screen` as the wrapper. No change is needed in these 29 files.
duplicates.fix: Add `analytics.track`, `analytics.identify` and `analytics.screen` from `@/analytics` to the tracking profile's wrapper list. Only `src/analytics/index.ts` should be treated as the adapter that may import the PostHog SDK. Don't change the call sites.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings point at the project's own tracking wrapper (script artefact)
duplicates.explanation: All 29 direct_sdk hits call `analytics.track` or `analytics.identify` with `analytics` imported from '@/analytics'. That is the `Analytics` class and singleton the app defines, not a vendor SDK, so these calls already go through the wrapper. The scanner most likely matched the `analytics.track(` call shape without recognising the import path. These are not real problems.
duplicates.fix: Teach the direct_sdk check that '@/analytics' is the adapter and exempt it. Then re-run the audit so any vendor SDK imports outside src/analytics show up on their own.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings are a script artefact: `analytics` from '@/analytics' is the wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 30 flagged lines call `analytics.track(analytics.event.X, ...)`, with `analytics` imported from '@/analytics'. That is the project's own `Analytics` class. It is the only place that imports the PostHog SDK and calls `client.capture`. It is typed against `EventProperties`, adds wallet metadata, honours doNotTrack and queues events until init. None of the flagged files import PostHog directly. The check most likely treats any `.track(` call as an SDK call because the wrapper's method name matches the SDK's. Fix the check or the tracking profile so `@/analytics` counts as the adapter. No code change is needed in these screens.
duplicates.fix: Add `src/analytics/index.ts` / the `analytics` export to the tracking profile as the wrapper, so these calls stop being flagged. Leave the call sites as they are.

duplicates.title: Event and property names break the naming pattern (R001, R007)
duplicates.explanation: The scripts flagged 42 event names. Many are older names in Title Case with spaces, such as 'Changed language' and 'Tapped "Done" after editing wallet', or dotted names such as learn_article.opened. The 138 flagged property names are camelCase, such as walletAddressHash, walletType and chainId. The analytics wrapper adds walletAddressHash and walletType to every event, so one wrapper change would cover most of the 138. This is hygiene only, and the pattern may be stricter than what this client's conventions allow.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename in place. Where the names matter, add the new name, mark the old event deprecated with replaced_by, and dual-fire for one release. For the wrapper properties, add snake_case versions alongside the camelCase ones. Otherwise, set the client's _conventions.yaml to accept the existing styles so the validator stops flagging them.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk flags are a script artefact: `analytics.track` is the tracking wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 28 flagged calls go through `analytics.track` imported from `@/analytics`. That is the project's own wrapper: the `Analytics` class in src/analytics/index.ts calls PostHog `capture` internally, and event names are typed from src/analytics/event.ts. None of them is an SDK call outside the adapter, so the flags are false positives. The scanner treats the wrapper's `.track` method name as a direct SDK call. The profile should list `analytics.track` as the wrapper.
duplicates.fix: Add `analytics` from `@/analytics` to the tracking profile's wrapper list so these calls stop being flagged. No code change is needed.

duplicates.title: Property names are mixed camelCase and snake_case, and some types differ between events
duplicates.explanation: The default convention is snake_case. This code sends camelCase property names such as branchCampaign, completedAt, walletStatus and totalSupply. At the same time, the SDK-injected appsflyer_id is snake_case. This is a naming inconsistency, not a defect. The R013 hits (the same name with different types) cannot be confirmed from the code I was given. The same property name, for example amount or chainId, is sent from many call sites with values computed in different places. I could not see which sites disagree. Check them before the next release, because type splits in the analytics tool cannot be fixed retroactively.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename existing properties in place. Set the naming pattern in _conventions.yaml to match the existing camelCase usage, so new properties follow one rule. For a type conflict, use a new property name and deprecate the old one. Do not change the type on the old name.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F70: duplicate of F70. The R013 type conflicts remain unchecked.

duplicates.title: Naming-pattern violations (R001/R007) come from the app's established dotted, camelCase convention
duplicates.explanation: The swap events use a `swaps.` namespace with a dot, and the properties are camelCase (`inputAssetAddress`, `walletAddressHash`). Both are used consistently across the app, and `quote_failed` is the only snake_case outlier. `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are added by the analytics wrapper to every event, which makes up most of the 90 property hits. So the hits are a mismatch with the default pattern, not defects in the swap code.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename. Renaming breaks history and needs deprecate plus `replaced_by` and dual-fire. Set the client's `_conventions.yaml` to accept the `domain.action` and camelCase patterns. Fix only the `quote_failed` snake_case properties if that event stays.

duplicates.title: Legacy event and property names break the naming pattern
duplicates.explanation: The event names are human-readable strings with spaces and quotes, such as 'Pressed Button' and 'Tapped "Send"'. claimable_panel.opened uses dots. The properties use camelCase (buttonName, walletAddressHash, walletType, chainId) where the pattern wants snake_case. Pressed Button's name comes from event.ts, and the camelCase properties are hard-coded at the call site or added by analytics.track. This is a naming and hygiene problem, not a bug.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename in place, because it would blank every existing report. For new events use object_action snake_case. For the old ones, either declare an exemption for them in _conventions.yaml or migrate each through a new event, deprecate the old one with replaced_by, and dual-fire for one release. Pressed Button is a generic catch-all keyed on buttonName. Over time, replace it with specific events that carry an entry_point.

duplicates.title: Dotted event names and camelCase property names break the plan's snake_case patterns
duplicates.explanation: The three events use the app's established object.action dotted style, for example 'card.pressed', and the properties are camelCase. The registry's event_pattern is snake_case object_action, and the default property pattern is snake_case. That produces the R001 error (3 events) and the R007 errors (12 properties, flagged as 14). The names are consistent with the rest of the app's event.ts and TypeScript schemas. Past data already sits under these names. The violation is a mismatch between the plan's convention and the code's. It isn't a bug in the call sites. Renaming in place would blank every report on these events. walletAddressHash and walletType come from the shared analytics wrapper, so renaming them would change every event, not only these three.
duplicates.fix: Prefer the non-breaking route. Widen event_pattern and the property pattern in analytics/registry/_conventions.yaml to allow dotted names and camelCase, which the analytics owner has to approve, or accept the exceptions. If you do want snake_case, go through deprecate + replaced_by with a dual-fire window of at least one release. Do the same for any event on a dashboard. Mobile installs that haven't updated keep sending the old names, so cut dashboards over by app version. Never rename in place. Don't rename the wrapper properties unless you do it for the whole app.

duplicates.title: camelCase property names come from shared analytics code, not from these events (R007)
duplicates.explanation: walletAddressHash and walletType are not passed by these calls. The analytics class adds them to every event from the wallet context, so the 8 hits on them are one cause repeated per event. eventSentAfterMs is a camelCase name defined in the event type and used in the NFT call. Renaming the injected properties would change every event in the product.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename. Treat walletAddressHash and walletType as shared context properties, set the project's convention to allow camelCase, or baseline them. Rename eventSentAfterMs only through a new property name with a dual-fire window (for example `duration_ms`). It measures the time before the event was sent, not time the person spent.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings are false positives: these calls go through the wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All eight flagged lines call analytics.track or analytics.identify, or track through the event alias. These are methods of the project's own Analytics class. That class is the adapter and is the only place that calls the PostHog client (client.capture, client.identify and client.screen). The scanner matched the method names track and identify and did not recognise the wrapper. Nothing here bypasses the adapter.
duplicates.fix: Add the analytics instance exported from src/analytics/index.ts to the tracking profile as the wrapper. Then the scanner stops flagging these calls.

duplicates.title: camelCase property names (`componentStack`, `eventId`, `walletAddressHash`, `walletType`) fail the property naming pattern
duplicates.explanation: `componentStack` and `eventId` are passed as camelCase keys by the two track() calls. `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are not passed by these calls. `analytics.track` adds them to every event from the stored wallet context (`getDefaultMetadata`). That is why R007 fires on the same two names across many other events. This is a repo-wide property naming style that disagrees with the snake_case pattern. It is not specific to the error boundary.
duplicates.fix: Settle the property convention once, at repo level. Either allow camelCase in `_conventions.yaml` (the wallet context properties are shared and widely used), or migrate to snake_case through new property names. Don't change the type or name of a property in place. Treat `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` as one shared decision, not as eight separate fixes.

duplicates.title: Mixed event and property naming (R001/R007), a legacy-vs-new split in the plan
duplicates.explanation: event.ts mixes Title Case names with spaces ('Approved new WalletConnect session', 'Showing Walletconnect signing request') and dotted lowercase names ('wc.failed_request', 'cash.*', 'browser.*'). Properties are camelCase (dappName, dappUrl, walletAddressHash, walletType), which triggers R007 on 501 properties. This is a naming-convention mismatch between the older and newer parts of the product, not a defect in what is sent. The 115 R001 findings are probably the same split. I have not checked each of them.
duplicates.fix: If the client's _conventions.yaml accepts these patterns, whitelist them. Otherwise do not rename in place. Use deprecate + replaced_by with a dual-fire window, because renaming breaks every report on the old names. Prefer to apply the new convention only to new events.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings are a script artefact: `analytics` is the tracking wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 28 flagged lines call `analytics.track(analytics.event.X, …)`. `analytics` is the app's own `Analytics` class. It is the single adapter around the PostHog client, and it adds the wallet, device and AppsFlyer metadata. Its `track()` takes only event names and property types declared in `@/analytics/event`. No flagged file imports the PostHog SDK. The scanner probably matched the `.track(` call shape. Nothing needs fixing in these files. The profile's wrapper list should include `analytics.track`, or the check should be silenced for these files.
duplicates.fix: Add `analytics.track` to the wrapper allow-list in the tracking profile and re-run the audit. Don't change the call sites.

duplicates.title: Naming hygiene: mixed casing and per-screen events
duplicates.explanation: Property names mix `wallet_label` (snake_case) with `isFirstWallet`, `chainId`, `durationSeconds` (camelCase), and the `device_*` metadata. Event keys are `tapped*`, `welcome*` and `show*`, which do not follow `object_action`. `showSecretView` is a screen view that carries a `category` of 'settings backup', and it is also a sensitive screen where the event name hints at the seed-phrase view. These settings and tap events could be one `setting_changed` event with a `setting` property, or one `button_tapped`. That is a rule 3 issue.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename in place. For new code use one casing. For existing events, add the new names, deprecate the old with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire where they are core events such as onboarding (`welcome*`).

duplicates.title: walletAddressHash, walletType and durationInMs are camelCase; the wallet two are added by the analytics wrapper, not by these call sites
items: Time spent on the Discover screen.walletAddressHash
Time spent on the Discover screen.walletType
Time spent on the Discover screen.durationInMs
duplicates.explanation: None of the three Discover call sites passes walletAddressHash or walletType. The analytics client merges them into every event as default metadata, from the wallet context. So the R007 hits on these two are mostly an artefact: the same pair repeats on every event in the registry. The value is a hash, not a raw address. They can be undefined before a wallet exists, which matches the `required: false` in the registry. `durationInMs` is set by the call site and is the only property the hook sends. It is a numeric latency in camelCase.
duplicates.fix: Keep the wallet context as a shared default-metadata entry in the registry (as utils.yaml already does) rather than repeating it on every event. Treat the casing as a convention exception for these properties and baseline them. Renaming a property needs a new name and a deprecation of the old one, never a retype. Leave `durationInMs` as is unless the whole project moves to snake_case.

duplicates.title: Naming rule failures come from the repo's own convention, not from broken events
duplicates.explanation: R001 and R007 compare against the default `object_action` snake_case pattern. This codebase uses Title Case event names ('Changed Chart Type', event.ts:314-315) and camelCase properties across the whole event map. The wallet properties are added to every event by `getDefaultMetadata` in analytics/index.ts:147-148. These are repo-wide conventions, not an error specific to these two events. Renaming them would split history and break existing reports.
duplicates.fix: Declare the real pattern in `_conventions.yaml`: Title Case event names and camelCase properties. That clears R001 and R007 without touching the code. Do not rename in place. If a rename is ever wanted, use deprecate + `replaced_by` and a dual-fire window.

duplicates.title: All 30 property_missing findings are script artefacts: the scanner attached the neighbouring event's call to each registry entry
duplicates.explanation: Each flagged property is sent by the right call. The scanner pointed at the wrong call in the same file, usually the success or failure sibling, so it compared the registry against the wrong property list. perps.withdraw.failed points at withdrawalConfig.ts:48, the perps.withdrew success call. Its real call is at line 57 and sends amount and errorMessage. predictions.place_order points at executePolymarketOrder.ts:353, which is the order_match.failed call. Its real call is at line 324 and sends averagePriceUsd, bestPriceUsd, feeAmountUsd, orderAmountUsd, orderPriceUsd and tokenAmount. predictions.order_match.failed points at line 324 but is sent at line 353 with orderId, reason, status and errorMessage. predictions.redeem_position.failed points at redeemPosition.ts:59, the success call. Its real call is at line 82 and sends errorMessage. rnbw_airdrop.claim.failed points at claimAirdrop.ts:91, the success call. It is really sent at lines 49 and 116, both with errorMessage. rnbw_airdrop.claim points at line 49, the failure call. It is really sent at line 91 with claimId, claimedRnbw, claimedValueInCurrency, decimals, pollAttempts and status. The TypeScript payload types in event.ts agree with the registry for all six events. No data snapshot was provided, so nothing is claimed about what arrives.
duplicates.fix: No change to the tracking code or the registry. Fix the scanner's call-to-event matching so it pairs each analytics.event.X constant with its own track call. This looks like an off-by-one when one function holds several track calls. Then re-run the audit.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F72: duplicate of F72. The real calls I read (claimAirdrop.ts:49/91/116, PolymarketNewPositionSheet:209) match.

duplicates.title: Naming-pattern failures are inherited names, not a tracking bug
duplicates.explanation: Both event names are fixed constants in the event table: 'performance.report' (dotted) and 'Performance Wallet Initialize Time' (Title Case). The properties are camelCase (durationInMs, performanceTrackingVersion), typed in the event property map and merged in by trackMetric. walletAddressHash and walletType come from the analytics default metadata. This is the repository's existing convention, which differs from the default object_action snake_case pattern. R001 and R007 are flagging the naming scheme, not broken calls. No data snapshot was given, so nothing is known about arriving volumes.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename in place. Either set the client's `_conventions.yaml` naming pattern to allow this scheme (or accept the existing baseline), or, if a rename is wanted, add the new event, mark the old one deprecated with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release (cut dashboards over by app version). Lowest-risk option: leave the names and accept the findings.

duplicates.title: property_missing findings are script artefacts: the real calls send entryMode, reason and mode
duplicates.explanation: The checker appears to have attached neighbouring tracking calls to the wrong event. Every flagged line is a different event's call: line 495 is cashWalletCheckFailed (flagged for amount_entered), line 477 is cashAmountEntered (flagged for wallet_check_failed), and lines 36, 47 and 55 are cashWalletLinked, cashPasskeySubmitted and cashPasskeyAdded, which carry no properties. The phone_submitted lines are cashPhoneSubmitFailed, cashPhoneAlreadyRegistered, cashExistingAccountRecoverySelected, cashKycAwaitingDecision, cashKycSubmitted, cashKycFailed and cashKycApproved. The actual calls all send the required property: cashAmountEntered sends entryMode, cashWalletCheckFailed, cashWalletLinkFailed and cashPasskeyFailed send reason from getTelemetryErrorReason, and cashPhoneSubmitted sends mode at all three sites (challenge.kind, 'resume', 'recovery'). No tracking is broken here.
duplicates.fix: Fix the scanner's call-to-event matching so each call is checked against its own event name only. Don't change the app code. Re-run the audit afterwards.

duplicates.title: All 30 property_missing flags are scanner artefacts: the checks read the wrong tracking call in each file
duplicates.explanation: The flags point at the wrong calls. For perps.opened_position the scanner cites lines 237 and 266. Line 237 is perpsOpenPositionCanceled and line 266 is perpsOpenPositionFailed. The real perpsOpenedPosition call is at line 249 and sends entryPrice, positionSize, positionValue and triggerOrders. The same mix-up happens for perps.closed_position, where the scanner cites 179, the perpsClosePositionFailed call. The real perpsClosedPosition call is at 150 and sends closePercentage, exitPrice, pnl, positionSize, positionValue and triggerOrders. For perps.trigger_order_created it cites 281, the perpsTriggerOrderFailed call. The real perpsTriggerOrderCreated call is at 268 and sends leverage and positionValue. For the failed events, errorMessage is sent at 266 (open failed) and 179 (close failed), but the scanner cites 237, 249 and 150. The scanner probably matches a call to an event by file and neighbouring call rather than by the exact event key. A second cause is that the drafted entries list properties as 'Not sent by this event' (errorMessage on success events, entryPrice and similar on failure events), so a property-list comparison can't tell what each call sends. In every flagged case the code sends the properties the registry declares as required. The registry is consistent with the code. Nothing about arriving data is known.
duplicates.fix: Fix the scanner so it resolves each call to its own event key and span, and ignores properties marked required:false or 'Not sent by this event'. Make no change to the code or the registry. In the registry, drop the 'Not sent by this event' placeholder properties from entries, so that each event lists only what its call sends.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F72: duplicate of F72. ClosePositionBottomSheet.tsx:150 and :179 send the properties claimed.

duplicates.title: Wallet profile and app-icon events carry little to break down by
duplicates.explanation: `walletProfileSubmitted` and `walletProfileCancelled` carry no properties, although `actionType` (Create or Edit) and `isFromSettings` are in scope in the handler. The two outcomes can't be split between creating and editing a profile. `handleSubmit` also fires the event before the keychain callback completes, so it records intent rather than success. The app-icon events do carry `appIcon`, but the unlock CTA event fires after a 500 ms delay and navigation, so it is lost if the user backs out in that window.
duplicates.fix: Add `action_type` and `is_from_settings` to the two wallet-profile events. This is additive and not breaking. Move the CTA track before the `delay`, and say in the registry that the wallet-profile submit is an intent.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F40: duplicate of F40. The CTA delay part is F100.

duplicates.title: property_missing flags are script artefacts: the flagged lines are not these events' calls
duplicates.explanation: All 30 findings point at lines that hold other events. In useSubmitReviewFlow.ts, lines 155, 176, 191, 227, 231 and 235 are cashKycAwaitingDecision, cashKycSubmitted, cashKycFailed and cashKycApproved. In useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts, line 190 is cashExistingAccountRecoverySelected. Line 68 is the cashPhoneSubmitted call, so it was also checked against the wrong events (reason, outcome). The scanner appears to have matched calls to events by line, not by event name. The real call sites send the required properties. cashPhoneSubmitted sends mode at useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts:68, useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:124 and verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:106. cashPhoneVerified sends mode at useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:91 and verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:127. cashPhoneSubmitFailed sends reason at useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts:78 and :154. cashPhoneAlreadyRegistered sends outcome at useSubmitPhoneFlow.ts:126 and :134. The event type map in event.ts (lines 573-592) makes these properties mandatory at compile time. No tracking change is needed. This isn't a code problem.
duplicates.fix: Fix the scanner's call-to-event matching so it keys on the event constant (analytics.event.X), not the line. Re-run the audit afterwards. Leave the code as it is.

duplicates.title: Failure is a separate event, and the stage of the failure can't be told apart
duplicates.explanation: Rule 4 puts success and failure on one outcome event, with `status` and `failure_reason`. Here each claim has a success event and a separate `.claim.failed` event, so claim conversion needs a union of two events. The registry question for rnbw_rewards.claim.failed asks 'at which stage', but no property carries it. The prepare and submit stages can only be told apart by whether intentId or claimId is present. errorMessage is a free-text Error.message, which makes it hard to group on.
duplicates.fix: Add a `stage` property (prepare | submit | poll) and a bounded `failure_reason` enum to the failure events now, which is additive. Moving to a single outcome event with status would change existing events. If you do it, go through deprecate + `replaced_by` and a dual-fire window, because claims are money events.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F8: duplicate of F8. The missing `stage` property is an addition.

duplicates.title: walletAddressHash and walletType are camelCase default properties added to every event
duplicates.explanation: The analytics wrapper adds these two properties to every event through `getDefaultMetadata`. They are not set at the call sites in the notifications code. The R007 failure comes from their camelCase names, and it applies to every event in the repo, not to these two events. The values are a hash and a type, not raw wallet addresses. The properties are optional, and undefined before a wallet exists.
duplicates.fix: Record them once as shared default properties in `_properties.yaml` and allow camelCase for them in the conventions, rather than listing them on each event. Renaming them to snake_case would split every report across all events, so it would need new property names and a dual-send window.

duplicates.title: All 30 property_missing flags are script artefacts: the scanner read the wrong call
duplicates.explanation: Every flagged line is a different event's call, not the event it was flagged for. AddWalletSheet.tsx:49 is tappedCreateNewWallet, which has no properties. The real addWalletFlowStarted calls are at :45, :59, :71 and :82, and each sends isFirstWallet and type. Airdrops/utils.ts:121, SponsoredClaimableContext.tsx:136 and TransactionClaimableContext.tsx:469 are claimClaimableSucceeded calls, which don't carry failureStep or errorMessage. Every claimClaimableFailed call (utils.ts:150, Sponsored 74/95/115/157/175, Transaction 417/440/491/515/534) sends both. LearnWebViewScreen.tsx:51 is learnArticleShared. The learnArticleOpened call at :35 sends displayType and routeName. ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:267 is tappedCancelEditingWallet. The Done call at :264 sends wallet_label. The scanner's call attribution needs fixing.

duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F72: duplicate of F72. AddWalletSheet.tsx:45/49 and ChangeWalletSheet.tsx:264/267 match.

duplicates.title: Event names use dots, spaces and quotes: legacy names that the pattern flags (R001)
duplicates.explanation: The names are string constants in the shared event map. They are sentence-style or dotted, not snake_case object_action. They are the names that go to the analytics tool, so existing reports depend on them.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename in place. If you want to rename, add a new event (for example `wallet_profile_submitted`, `wallet_profile_cancelled`, `nft_details_viewed`), mark the old one `deprecated` with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release. Otherwise record the names as accepted legacy in the baseline or conventions.

duplicates.title: Naming-pattern errors on app_store_review.prompted come from the repo's own convention, not a tracking bug
duplicates.explanation: The event name uses a dotted `area.action` form. The app already uses that form for 141 event names in event.ts, so the default `object_action` snake_case pattern doesn't fit this client. The properties `promptCount`, `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are camelCase in code. `action` and `promptCount` are in the event schema. The wallet fields are default metadata that the analytics client adds to every event, as the analytics tests show. The event is sent from one place, promptForReview, right after `StoreReview.requestReview()` resolves. It is not sent if the call throws. The scripts flag these four items only because the repo's `_conventions.yaml` pattern doesn't match the app's naming. Setting the pattern in `_conventions.yaml` to allow dotted names and camelCase properties would clear all four. Renaming the event or its properties is a breaking change. If the team wants the rename anyway, add a new event, mark the old one `deprecated` with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release. A type or name change on `promptCount` needs a new property name. Nothing is known about arriving data because there is no snapshot.
duplicates.fix: Configure the client's `_conventions.yaml` to accept dotted event names and camelCase properties, and exempt the default wallet metadata (`walletAddressHash`, `walletType`). Don't rename the live event just to satisfy the default pattern. If a rename is wanted later, go through deprecate + `replaced_by` and a dual-fire window.

duplicates.title: Registry entries list properties that belong to other events
duplicates.explanation: The drafts took properties from neighbouring calls. cash.amount_entered lists `reason`, which only cash.wallet_check_failed sends (AddCashSheet.tsx:495). cash.wallet_check_failed lists `amount` and `entryMode`, which only cash.amount_entered sends (AddCashSheet.tsx:477-480). cash.phone_submitted lists `outcome` (sent by cash.phone_already_registered), `reason` (sent by cash.phone_submit_failed) and `source` (sent by cash.kyc_awaiting_decision). The real phone_submitted calls send only `mode`. The registry says the events carry properties they never send, and a failed property check on any of these would be a false alarm.
duplicates.fix: Remove the properties that these events don't send: `reason` from amount_entered, `amount` and `entryMode` from wallet_check_failed, and `outcome`, `reason` and `source` from phone_submitted. Keep `mode` required on phone_submitted. Make no change to the code.

The resend-failure call is at line 194 and sends `{reason, mode}`, and the store test at verifyPhoneFlowStore.test.ts:637 asserts it. (2) `request.approved` was linked to SignTransactionSheet.tsx:295. That line is inside `onCancel` and tracks `txRequestReject` (`request.rejected`), which has no dappName, dappUrl or network. The approve calls are at lines 406 and 511 (transaction and signature). Both send source, requestType, dappName, dappUrl, isHardwareWallet and network. (3) `Rap failed` was linked to six calls in ens/raps/actions.ts, at lines 394, 400, 422, 428, 434 and 440. The real `ensRapFailed` call is at actions.ts:689 and sends category, failed_action and label. The likely cause is that the scanner matched calls by position or proximity, not by the event constant. Then re-run the audit and expect these 30 findings to clear. No code or registry change is needed, and nothing is renamed, so no deprecation or dual-fire window applies.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F72: duplicate of F72. actions.ts:689 sends category, failed_action and label, and SignTransactionSheet:295 is the reject call.

duplicates.title: status without failure_reason on the predictions and rnbw claim events (R012)
duplicates.explanation: Each of these has both a main event and a '.failed' variant: predictions.place_order and .failed, rnbw_airdrop.claim and .failed, rnbw_rewards.claim and .failed. Where a status property exists, no failure_reason accompanies it. The same split as in the cash flow applies. This is based on the declared event names and the scanner results. duplicates.title: Event and property names break the snake_case `object_action` pattern (R001/R007)
duplicates.explanation: The three event names contain dots: `performance.time_to_sign`, `performance.time_to_sign.operation` and `wallet_initialization.failed`. The properties are camelCase (completedAt, elapsedTime, totalElapsedTime, timeToCompletion, resultWasNullish, walletType, and others). That is the naming style of this codebase's whole analytics layer, not a mistake at one call site. The names are defined as constants and typed once. The R007 hits are all the same two events' fields. wallet_initialization.failed also puts a failure on its own `.failed` event. The rules prefer `status` on an outcome event, but there is no initialization outcome event to hold it.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename in place, because reports on the old names would go blank. The cheapest fix is to record these as an explicit exception in `_conventions.yaml`, or to allow dotted and camelCase names. If they are renamed, add the new event, mark the old one deprecated with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release. That also applies to any dashboard on the time-to-sign pair. Cut over by app version.

duplicates.title: Two events fire for one tap on the add-wallet sheet
duplicates.explanation: Each button on AddWalletSheet fires a `tapped…` event and `addWalletFlowStarted` with `type` ('new' or 'seed'). The two carry the same information. This is the same action from the same place reported twice, and one of them already has the property that tells the cases apart.
duplicates.fix: Keep addWalletFlowStarted with `type` and deprecate the tapped* events. Don't remove them at once. Dual-fire for a release, then retire them.

duplicates.title: camelCase properties fail the property naming rule; two of them are added by the analytics wrapper, not by this call
duplicates.explanation: `sessionId` is passed by the deeplink handler in camelCase. `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are not in this call at all. `analytics.track` merges them into every event from the wallet context (`this.walletAddressHash`, `this.walletType`). R007 is therefore really about the shared wrapper vocabulary, not about this handler. The same two names appear on many registry entries, and they are baselined. `walletType` can be undefined, for example right after wallet creation. Because they are optional, they can be missing on some events. `sessionId` is the join key to `f2c.provider.flow_opened` and `f2c.transaction_received`, so renaming it on one event only would break the join.
duplicates.fix: Treat the wallet context properties as one shared decision. Either allow camelCase in the property pattern, or add a baseline exception covering them. Keep `sessionId` unchanged across the whole f2c flow. A rename would need a new property name carried by every f2c event during a dual-fire window, because a property can't be renamed in place.

duplicates.title: Three Discover events use legacy human-readable names instead of the object_action pattern
items: Time spent on the Discover screen
duplicates.explanation: The names are the string values in the event map: 'Search Query', 'Tapped Search' and 'Time spent on the Discover screen'. They are mixed-case phrases with spaces, not snake_case. Each has exactly one call site, and each is already in the baseline of accepted R001 violations. The names are inconsistent but not broken. Each event fires from a single place, so there are no casing splits.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename in place, because reports on the old names would go blank. If a rename is wanted, add new events (for example `discover_search_cleared`, `discover_search_tapped`, `discover_screen_time_spent`). Mark the old entries deprecated with `deprecated_reason` and `replaced_by`. Dual-fire for one release and cut dashboards over by app version, since old mobile installs keep sending the old names. Otherwise keep the names and leave the baseline as it is.

duplicates.title: R007 on add_favorite_token is a naming-convention mismatch: the properties are camelCase like the rest of the codebase, and two are added by the analytics client
duplicates.explanation: The three properties fail the snake_case property pattern, but nothing is broken. `chainId` is passed by the call site and typed as camelCase in the event payload. `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are not passed by the call site. `getDefaultMetadata` adds them to every event, and `capture` merges them in. So the names are the analytics client's shared vocabulary, not a one-off choice for this event. The client already mixes conventions: the Android device fields are snake_case (`device_brand`) and `appsflyer_id` is too. `_conventions.yaml` only overrides `event_pattern`, so the default snake_case property rule applies to a codebase that is camelCase throughout. The registry's shared `_properties.yaml` has about 150 camelCase property names, so this is a convention-level mismatch rather than a bug in this event. Renaming only these three would split the property from every other event that carries it. I can't say how the data looks, because there is no snapshot.
duplicates.fix: Do not rename in code. Either declare a camelCase `property_pattern` in `_conventions.yaml` (an analytics-owner decision) or accept R007 for these names. Document `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` once, as auto-added default properties, rather than as per-event properties on each of the 227 events. If a rename to snake_case is ever wanted, it is breaking: add new property names, dual-send for one release, and deprecate the old ones. Don't retype or rename them in place.

duplicates.title: Event names debug.identify_probe and 'First App Open' don't match the naming pattern

'First App Open' is a first-value/onboarding event. Set a removal date in the registry so the probe doesn't stay live. Also fix the stale 'Amplitude' mention in the App.tsx:175-176 comment: the client is PostHog.

duplicates.title: Event names are Title Case with spaces, so they fail R001

duplicates.title: property_missing findings are a script and registry artefact: the two signing events were swapped and cross-listed
duplicates.explanation: The code is consistent. The operation event is sent at line 62 with the whole `log` object (completedAt, screen, operation, startTime, endTime, metadata, timeToCompletion, resultWasNullish). The end-of-flow event is sent at line 69 with only screen, completedAt, elapsedTime, totalElapsedTime and error. The scanner read the literal object at line 69 as if it belonged to the operation event. It read the `log` call at line 62 as if it belonged to time_to_sign. That is why elapsedTime and totalElapsedTime are reported 'missing' at :62 and endTime, operation, startTime, timeToCompletion and resultWasNullish are reported 'missing' at :69. The drafted registry makes it worse. Each entry lists the other event's properties as optional, with the description 'Not sent by this event'. Those entries are not real properties of that event. The properties walletType and walletAddressHash are added by the analytics client, not at these call sites. This audit did not check them.
duplicates.fix: Remove the cross-listed 'Not sent by this event' properties from both registry entries. time_to_sign keeps screen, completedAt, elapsedTime, totalElapsedTime and error. The operation event keeps the PerformanceLog fields. Then make the scanner match each call to its own event, so a call that passes a variable like `log` is resolved from its type. No change to the tracking calls is needed.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F75: duplicate of F75. performance.ts:62 sends `log` and :69-75 sends the end-of-flow fields.

duplicates.title: Dotted event names (`error_boundary.viewed`, `error_boundary.reset`) don't match the plan's naming pattern
duplicates.explanation: The names are defined in src/analytics/event.ts as `domain.action` strings. The repo uses this style for its events (for example `perps.withdrew`). `_conventions.yaml` sets `event_pattern` to `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+$`, which allows no dots. So R001 fires on the convention, not on a bug in this call site. Both calls are live: ErrorBoundary.tsx calls track() for each event on the Sentry `onError` and `onReset` callbacks. No data snapshot was provided, so nothing is known about arriving data.
duplicates.fix: Prefer to change `event_pattern` in `_conventions.yaml` to allow the dotted `domain.action` style that the whole codebase already uses. That change goes to the analytics owner. Do not rename these events in code just to satisfy the lint. A rename breaks any report on the old names. If a rename is still wanted, add the new event, mark the old one `deprecated` with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release (the crash-funnel `viewed` and `reset` pair is on a dashboard).

duplicates.title: Wallet create events use a dotted name the naming pattern rejects (script/convention mismatch, not a wallet bug)
duplicates.explanation: The names are fixed literals in src/analytics/event.ts (walletCreateSucceeded and walletCreateFailed). They use the `object.action` dotted style. `_conventions.yaml` sets `event_pattern` to `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+$`, which allows only underscores, so R001 fires. The baseline lists 222 R001 event entries, so this is the repository's long-standing naming style and not something specific to these two events. The calls work: each is sent from createWallet in src/model/wallet.ts. Which name the data actually carries is unknown, because there is no snapshot. Renaming only to satisfy the linter would blank every report on the old names.
duplicates.fix: Choose one of two routes with the analytics owner. (a) Leave the names alone and widen `event_pattern` in `_conventions.yaml` to allow `.` as a separator, which covers the whole family of 222 events. (b) Rename to `wallet_create_succeeded` / `wallet_create_failed`. That is breaking: add the new events, mark the old entries `deprecated` with `replaced_by`, dual-fire for one release (`dual_fire_until`), add a `SEMANTICS:` changelog line, and cut dashboards over by app version. Better still, follow rule 4 and fold both into one outcome event such as `wallet_created` with `status` and `failure_reason`, as part of the same migration. Never rename in place.

duplicates.title: Wallet Profile submit and cancel have no start event, so no rate can be computed
duplicates.explanation: Submit is sent first in handleSubmit, before onCloseModal and before the keychain callback for 'Create'. A failure after the tap is not tracked, and there is no event for opening the modal. Cancel is sent after goBack. The two events are both intent-style taps. Neither can show how many people opened the modal and left, or how many saves failed.
duplicates.fix: Add a modal-opened event. Send an outcome event from the keychain callback, or from the save path, with a `status` property.

duplicates.title: Send amount-input events fire on every keystroke and carry no value information
items: Changed native currency input in Send flow
Changed token input in Send flow
duplicates.explanation: Both handlers send the event on every change of the field, so typing one amount sends many events. Counts reflect keystrokes, not people changing the amount.
duplicates.fix: Send once when the input settles (debounce or on blur) and only if the value changed. Or drop them in favour of the send-submitted event.

duplicates.title: probe/value 'missing' is a script artefact: the flagged line is the First App Open call, not the probe calls
duplicates.explanation: The property_missing checks point at src/App.tsx:198, which is `analytics.track(analytics.event.firstAppOpen)`. That event has no properties by design (event.ts types it as `undefined`). The `EventProperties` type makes both properties required. The reference was probably attributed to the wrong call site, so the 4 property_missing findings aren't real. Fix the scanner attribution, or re-point the references to App.tsx:177 and settings.ts:121.
duplicates.fix: No code change needed. Point the registry references at App.tsx:177 and src/redux/settings.ts:121, and mark `probe` and `value` as required in the registry.

duplicates.title: swaps.failed errorMessage is free text from the swap error
duplicates.explanation: errorMessage is the raw string returned by the rap and is sent as is. Elsewhere in the same file the code splits on '[' before showing it to the user, which suggests the raw string can contain extra detail (bracketed payloads). It is not confirmed that this includes user data. The raw text also makes breakdowns by error high-cardinality. No data was available to check the real values.
duplicates.fix: Check what the rap puts in errorMessage. Then send a normalised failure_reason enum, or the same truncated prefix the alert uses (split on '['), instead of the raw string. Treat it as a new property name alongside the old one, not a retype.

duplicates.title: Script artefact: the property check read the wrong call site (swaps.selected_asset), not swaps.submitted
duplicates.explanation: All 30 property_missing findings point at swap-provider.tsx:1023. That line is analytics.track(analytics.event.swapsSelectedAsset, {asset, otherAsset, type}), a different event. swaps.submitted is sent through trackSwapEvent(), which builds every flagged property (degenMode, errorMessage, inputAsset*, outputAsset*, isBridge, isHardwareWallet, isSwappingToPopularAsset, mainnetAddress, tradeAmountUSD, type) and calls analytics.track(event, params). duplicates.title: Registry entry for swaps.submitted lists properties it never sends (asset, otherAsset, parameters)
duplicates.explanation: The draft copied `asset`, `otherAsset` and `parameters` onto swaps.submitted. The first two belong to swaps.selected_asset (the call at swap-provider.tsx:1023). `parameters` is only read inside trackSwapEvent and is not in the params object. The registry marks them required:false, but they will show as properties that never arrive. The same cross-contamination is probably what pulled the wrong call reference in.
duplicates.fix: Remove `asset`, `otherAsset` and `parameters` from the swaps.submitted entry, or mark them deprecated, and add a changelog line. The entry is otherwise accurate. The event is typed in event.ts:771.

duplicates.title: Property-missing errors on Pressed Button are scanner misattribution
duplicates.explanation: The 28 property_missing errors for action and buttonName point to lines 264, 267, 286, 295, 317, 341 and 411 of ChangeWalletSheet.tsx. Those lines call other events: tappedDoneEditingWallet, tappedCancelEditingWallet, tappedEditWallet, tappedNotificationSettings, tappedDeleteWallet, tappedDeleteWalletConfirm and tappedEdit. duplicates.title: Scanner attributed other events' calls to cash.phone_verify_failed; the two real calls are complete
duplicates.explanation:
The scanner picked up calls to other events as cash.phone_verify_failed and then flagged them for missing `mode` or `reason`. It also flagged `reason` values that are not in the enum. Only two calls in the code send cash.phone_verify_failed, and both carry `mode` and `reason`. (1) useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:101 sends `{mode:'recovery', reason:'client_error'}`. (2) verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:155-158 sends `reason: getTelemetryErrorReason(e)` and `mode: challenge.kind`. The flagged lines are other events:
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:91 is cashPhoneVerified.
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:124 is cashPhoneSubmitted.
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:155 is cashKycAwaitingDecision.
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:176 is cashKycSubmitted.
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:191, 231 and 235 are cashKycFailed. These produced the 'state_not_supported' and 'rejected' value_not_allowed errors. Those reasons belong to cash.kyc_failed, not to the phone event.
- useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:227 is cashKycApproved.
- verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:106 is cashPhoneSubmitted.
- verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:127 is cashPhoneVerified.
The typed payload in src/analytics/event.ts:593-596 also requires exactly `reason` and `mode`. No snapshot is available, so nothing is known about what arrives.
duplicates.fix: Treat all 30 property_missing and value_not_allowed findings as false positives and change nothing in the code. In the scanner, match calls by the event constant on the same call, not by nearby lines. Also remove the stray optional `source` property from the registry entry, because that property belongs to cash.kyc_awaiting_decision. The registry entry is correct to say `reason` is 'client_error' for a wrong recovery code. No rename or deprecation is needed.

duplicates.title: cash.kyc_failed 'reason missing' is a script artefact: the flagged lines are other KYC events
duplicates.explanation: The scanner linked cash.kyc_failed to lines that call other events. useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:227 is cashKycApproved, which has no properties. kycStatusService.ts:22 is cashKycApproved and :23 is cashKycAwaitingDecision, which sends `source`. Every real cash.kyc_failed call sends `reason`. Those calls are useSubmitReviewFlow.ts:191 (technical reason), :231 (state_not_supported) and :235 (rejected), and kycStatusService.ts:24 and :25. The type at event.ts:602 makes `reason` mandatory. The call-site references are off by a few lines, so the check compared the wrong calls. No tracking problem here.

duplicates.title: cash.sign_in_failed 'reason missing' is a script artefact: the flagged lines are the submitted, succeeded and cancelled calls

duplicates.title: cash.buy_completed 'properties missing' is a script artefact: the flagged lines are cash.buy_failed calls

duplicates.title: cash.phone_resend_failed 'reason' flagged missing at a call that belongs to cash.phone_submitted
duplicates.explanation: The report cites verifyPhoneFlowStore.ts:106. That line is the cash.phone_submitted call, which sends only { mode: 'recovery' }. Separately, confirm that getTelemetryErrorReason returns only the values listed in the registry (offline | client_error | server_error | unknown). The registry marks these values as drafted from code and they haven't been checked against arriving data.

duplicates.title: property_missing flags are a script artefact: only line 222 sends this event

duplicates.title: property_missing flags on 'Show wallet profile modal for imported wallet' are a script artefact: they point at other events' calls

duplicates.title: property_missing flags on 'Scanned broken or unsupported QR code' are a script artefact: they point at other scan events

duplicates.explanation: Lines 57, 78 and 105 are the calls for qrCodeScannedAddress, qrCodeScannedProfile and qrCodeScannedWalletConnect. All three are declared with `undefined` properties, so they correctly send none. The real call for the invalid-scan event is at line 124, in handleScanInvalid. It sends `qrCodeData`, which matches the declared type `{ qrCodeData: string }`. The property is not missing. The scanner attributed the neighbouring handlers' calls to the invalid-scan entry.

duplicates.title: Derived wallet address is sent raw while the wrapper already adds a hash
items: Show wallet profile modal for imported wallet
duplicates.explanation: The call at line 279 sends `address`, the address derived from the user's seed phrase or private key, in plain text. The analytics wrapper already attaches `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` to every event. The plain address is a stable on-chain identifier that links the analytics profile to the user's public wallet. `type` is just walletResult.type, and its values are unconfirmed in the code available. This is a hygiene issue and does not leak the secret. I have not verified how the wrapper or the project treats raw addresses elsewhere.

Document the values of `type` from deriveAccountFromWalletInput in the registry. Treat removing `address` as a modification of an existing event and note it in the changelog.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F1: duplicate of F1. Its evidence, line 279, is already in F1.

duplicates.title: property_missing on backup 'label' is a script artefact: the flagged calls are different events
duplicates.explanation: The checker blamed lines 66 and 74 for a missing `label` on 'Error updating Backup status'. Those lines are the calls for viewHowToEnableICloud ('View how to Enable iCloud') and ignoreHowToEnableICloud ('Ignore how to enable iCloud'). Their typed payload is only `{category}`, so nothing is missing. The real 'Error updating Backup status' call is at line 152 and does send `category` and `label`. The two events that actually fire at 66 and 74 have no registry entry of their own in the part given to me. The same applies to 'iCloud not enabled' at line 56.
duplicates.fix: Fix the scanner's event attribution so each call is matched to its own event name. Add registry entries for 'View how to Enable iCloud' and 'Ignore how to enable iCloud' (properties: category). Don't change the code.

duplicates.title: add_wallet_flow.started mixes methods and hard-codes isFirstWallet
duplicates.explanation: Restore-from-cloud sends type 'seed', the same as restore-from-seed, so the two methods can't be told apart. The event type allows 'backup' but no call sends it. The hardware-wallet option and ViewWalletBackup hard-code isFirstWallet: false, so first-wallet counts only reflect the three sheet paths. The registry description records both facts. The event also records intent only, since it fires on the tap before navigation.
duplicates.fix: Add a 'cloud' value to type (additive, so not breaking) and send it from restore-from-cloud. Keep 'seed' for seed-phrase import. Add an entry_point property to separate the Add Wallet sheet from ViewWalletBackup, and pass the real isFirstWallet where it is known.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings are a script artefact: `analytics` is the project's own wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 29 direct_sdk hits are calls to `analytics.track(...)` or `analytics.identify(...)` imported from `@/analytics`. That object is the wrapper class instance (`export const analytics = new Analytics()`). Only the class talks to PostHog (`client.capture`, `client.identify`), and it adds device and wallet metadata. Its `track` is typed against `EventProperties`, so each call is checked against the event schema. The scanner's profile appears not to recognise this wrapper, so none of the 29 sites bypasses it. The registry is empty for this run, but that does not make the calls missing or wrong.
duplicates.fix: Add `analytics` (from `@/analytics`, methods `track`, `identify`, `screen`) to the tracking profile as the adapter and re-run the scan. Don't change any call sites.

duplicates.title: NFT detail event sends the NFT name and image URL and fires for every NFT viewed for 5 seconds
duplicates.explanation: After a 5-second timeout in `UniqueTokenExpandedState`, `tokenDetailsNFT` sends `name` and `image_url` (low-res URL) with the contract address and chain. For ENS names this is a human-readable name tied to a wallet hash from the default metadata. The data is public on chain, but it is high-cardinality and not useful for breakdowns. Because the name is the NFT's, it is not raw user text. A 5-second dwell is also an arbitrary definition of 'viewed'.
duplicates.fix: Drop `name` and `image_url` and send `is_ens`, `is_poap`, `chain_id` and the contract address. Document the 5-second dwell as the firing moment in the registry description.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk flags are a script artefact: these calls already go through the project's tracking wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 29 flagged lines call `analytics.track(...)` from `@/analytics`. That is the app's own adapter, a singleton `Analytics` class. It is the only place that touches `PostHog.capture`, and it adds device and wallet metadata, queues events until init, and honours doNotTrack. The scanner matched `.track(` on the name `analytics` and did not recognise the wrapper. The real code-level risk is elsewhere (see the other findings). Add `analytics.track` / `@/analytics` to the tracking profile's wrapper list so these stop being reported.
duplicates.fix: No code change. Register `@/analytics` (`analytics.track`, `analytics.identify`) as the wrapper in the tracking profile and re-run the scan.

duplicates.title: direct_sdk findings are a script artefact: these calls already go through the tracking wrapper
duplicates.explanation: All 29 flagged lines call `analytics.track(analytics.event.X)`. `analytics` is the project's own wrapper (`export const analytics = new Analytics()` in src/analytics/index.ts). Its `track()` checks the event name against `EventProperties`. It also adds wallet metadata and the AppsFlyer id, and only then calls PostHog `capture`. The only direct PostHog use is inside the wrapper. The scanner most likely matches the `.track(` method name and not the SDK import. No call in the listed files imports `posthog-react-native`. Nothing needs changing in the call sites. The scanner profile should treat `@/analytics` as the adapter so these stop being reported.
duplicates.fix: Add `@/analytics` (the `analytics` export) to the tracking profile's adapter list and re-run the scan. No code change in the flagged files.

duplicates.title: tokenList event re-fires whenever the asset list changes
duplicates.explanation: The effect depends on `sortedAssets`, which comes from a live store (`legacyUserAssets`). It re-runs and re-tracks whenever the list or loading state updates, not once per screen open. The counts `no_icon`, `no_price` and `total_tokens` are then repeated per session. `no_price` counts a missing 24h change (`relative_change_24h`), not a missing price, so the property name is misleading.
duplicates.fix: Guard the effect so it fires once per mount (a ref flag). Fix the `no_price` computation or rename the property under a new name. Do not retype the existing property in place.

duplicates.title: f2cProviderFlowCompleted treats a deeplink return as a success for Ramp, and has no outcome for other providers
duplicates.explanation: The Ramp branch hard-codes `success: true` because returning via the deeplink is assumed to mean a purchase. The code comments say this. The other providers send the event with `success` undefined. The same event name therefore holds 'completed', 'returned' and 'unknown' states, and a conversion rate built on it overstates success. Abandonment (no return deeplink) leaves no event, which is the intent-without-outcome case from rule 2.
duplicates.fix: Rename the meaning in the description: this is 'returned from provider', not 'completed'. When a provider confirms the outcome, send it from the server or SDK callback with `status`. Document the Ramp assumption in the registry.

duplicates.title: Temporary debug probe event is still live
duplicates.explanation: A debug event, `debug.identify_probe`, fires alongside identify. The comment says to remove it after FEPLAT-67. It carries a `probe` and `value` pair, so it is an event used as a log line. Once the investigation ends it only adds noise and volume.
duplicates.fix: Remove the call when FEPLAT-67 closes. In the same PR, mark the event deprecated in the registry. Don't delete the entry.

duplicates.title: Event name uses a dotted namespace, not the object_action snake_case pattern (R001)
duplicates.explanation: The name is the value of `f2cProviderFlowCompleted` in the event map. It uses dots as a namespace (`f2c.provider.flow_completed`), but `event_pattern` allows only lowercase snake_case segments joined by `_`. This is a codebase-wide convention, not a one-off. The baseline already lists 91 dotted event names under R001. The call is live: it is sent from the `/f2c` deeplink handler, so this is naming hygiene and not broken tracking.
duplicates.fix: Don't rename it in place. Reports on the name and the intent/outcome pair (`f2c.provider.flow_opened`, `f2c.transaction_received`) would go blank. Either widen `event_pattern` to allow dots, which matches how the project already names events, or keep the baseline exception. If it is ever renamed, add the new event, mark this one `deprecated` with `replaced_by`, and dual-fire for one release. Mobile installs that haven't updated keep sending the old name for weeks, so cut dashboards over by app version.

duplicates.title: Registry draft for wallet_create.succeeded lists an `error` property the code never sends
duplicates.explanation: The success call passes `analyticsParams`, which has no `error` key. The registry entry itself notes that the draft lists `error` but the success call never sends it. The type in event.ts also adds `error` only to the failed event. R023 flags the same mismatch in the baseline. `walletAddressHash` and `walletType` are added by analytics.track from the stored wallet context. The registry entries are marked UNCONFIRMED and may be undefined for a brand-new wallet. This is not verified in data.
duplicates.fix: Remove `error` from the wallet_create.succeeded properties in `analytics/registry/model.yaml`. Check whether `walletType` and `walletAddressHash` are set before the success call for a first wallet. If not, pass them explicitly in `analyticsParams`.
duplicates.verifier_note: repeats F75: duplicate of F75. wallet.ts:722 sends analyticsParams with no error key.

duplicates.title: Search Query fires only when the input is cleared, not once per search
duplicates.explanation: The name suggests one event per search performed. The only call is in handleClearInput, which runs when the clear button is pressed with more than 1 character typed. Searches that end by submitting, cancelling or leaving the screen send nothing. Searches of 1 character are also skipped. The plan describes this behaviour, so the event is a count of cleared searches. Anyone using it as search volume or result-engagement will undercount it.
duplicates.fix: If search volume is the question, send the event when the query settles (debounced, once per changed value) or when the person leaves search. Otherwise rename or describe it as a cleared search so nobody reads it as total searches.

duplicates.title: add_new_wallet_group.name fires on the submit tap, even with an empty name, and sends the typed name
duplicates.explanation: The event is sent at the start of handleSubmit. This is before onCloseModal and goBack, and nothing checks the value first. An empty or whitespace-only name still fires it. Any count of this event is therefore a count of submit taps, not of wallet groups created. The name is also raw user text sent as a property, which the design rules say never to send. The tracked value is trimmed but the saved value (`name: value`) is not, so the two can differ.
duplicates.fix: Treat it as an intent event and add an outcome event, or move it to where the group is actually created. Skip or flag empty names. Replace `name` with `char_count` or a boolean such as `has_name`.

duplicates.title: token_details.nft fires on unmount as well as at 5 seconds, and the cancelled flag is ignored
duplicates.explanation: useTimeoutEffect calls the callback at 5 seconds with cancelled=false. If the sheet unmounts earlier, the cleanup calls it again with cancelled=true and a shorter elapsedTime. The handler never reads `cancelled`, so the two cases look the same in the data. The event does not mean the person saw the NFT at a specific moment. It fires once per mount, because the cleanup only calls the callback when less than 5 seconds have passed.
duplicates.fix: Read `cancelled` in the callback and send it as a property. Or ignore early unmounts if the 5-second view is what you mean to count.

duplicates.title: request.rejected mixes user rejections with signing failures, and skips some failures
duplicates.explanation: onCancel always sends the reject event. It is called when the person rejects, and also when sending or signing a transaction fails or message signing returns no result (onCancel(response?.error)). Failures are counted as rejections, and nothing separates them. For hardware wallets a failed transaction doesn't call onCancel, so no event is sent at all. The reject rate therefore overstates what people decided and misses part of the failed hardware-wallet requests.
duplicates.fix: Send a status property (rejected or failed) on the event, set from whether an error was passed to onCancel. Also send the event on the hardware-wallet failure path.

duplicates.title: Changed Global Notification Settings is unreachable today: no global topics exist
duplicates.explanation: The call sits behind `toggleGlobalNotificationTopic`, which sends the event only after a successful publish, which is the right moment. But `GlobalNotificationTopic` is an empty object, so `GlobalNotificationTopicType` has no values. `toggleTopic` in NotificationsSection is defined but nothing calls it, and there is no topic to toggle. The event can't fire, so any dashboard on it will stay at zero. The `topic` property can't carry a value either.
duplicates.fix: Deprecate the event and remove the dead call path if no global topics are coming back. If a topic is added later, the event will fire correctly after success without other changes.

duplicates.title: Received wc connection sends waitingTime as a number or an error string
duplicates.explanation: When receivedTimestamp is missing, waitingTime becomes the string 'Error calculating waiting time.'. Otherwise it is a number. The same property then has two types, which breaks averages and may split the property in the analytics tool. The effect also re-runs, and re-sends the event, when dappName, dappUrl or receivedTimestamp change.
duplicates.fix: Omit waitingTime (or send null) when the value can't be computed, and guard the effect with a ref so it sends once per sheet.

duplicates.title: token_launcher.image_upload_failed sends url and isModerated that are always undefined
duplicates.explanation: url and isModerated are assigned only after the success check inside the try. In the catch they are always undefined, so those two properties never carry a value.
duplicates.fix: Remove url and isModerated from the failure event, or send something known at failure time, such as the file size bucket.

duplicates.title: token_launcher.share_pressed fires after the share sheet closes, whether or not the person shared
duplicates.explanation: The event is sent after await Share.share(...) resolves, which happens on dismissal as well as on completion. It is named for the tap but sent after the sheet closes. If Share.share throws, nothing is sent, so taps are undercounted and shares are overcounted.
duplicates.fix: Send it before Share.share if it measures the tap. If it should measure an actual share, check the result's action (sharedAction vs dismissedAction) and record that.

duplicates.title: token_list fires several times per visit
duplicates.explanation: The wallet sender runs in an effect keyed on sortedAssets, so every asset refresh sends a new snapshot. The swap sender re-runs on data.results and is throttled to once per 5 s, so one search can still send several. Counts of token_list events will track data refreshes, not visits.
duplicates.fix: Send once per mount or visit (a ref guard), or document that the event is a data-refresh snapshot and don't count it as a visit.
