Disconnect from a dapp on `Routes.DAPP_BROWSER_CONTROL_PANEL` (secondary) has no event: It is the same action as the WalletConnect disconnect, so one event with a source property separates the two surfaces. It fires in handleDisconnect after removeAppSession. Existing rows get no source value. Add `source`, `dappUrl`.

Turn notifications on or off for a wallet on `Routes.WALLET_NOTIFICATIONS_SETTINGS` (secondary) has no event: The master switch in `toggleAllowNotifications` is the same kind of action as the existing event, a settings change with subscribe or unsubscribe. A new `scope` property and a `topic` of `all` answer how many wallets turn notifications off, split by owned and watched. Fire it only after `toggleGroupNotifications` succeeds. The name says 'Global', so rename it if the plan allows. Add `scope`, `topic`, `action`, `walletAddressHash`, `walletType`.

Back up wallet manually (view secret warning) on `Routes.VIEW_WALLET_BACKUP` (core) has no event: onManualBackup sends the person to SECRET_WARNING with isBackingUp, and the same secret view later renders. Adding isBackingUp to Show Secret View separates manual backups from plain secret views. Backup Complete already records the outcome, so no new event is needed. Add `isBackingUp`, `backupType`.

Create and confirm a PIN on `Routes.PIN_AUTHENTICATION_SCREEN`; Enter PIN to authenticate on `Routes.PIN_AUTHENTICATION_SCREEN` (core) has no event. The question is how many people who start setting a PIN finish it, and how often the confirm step is mismatched. Fire it once when the screen finishes: on onSuccess, on onCancel (the unmount cleanup when `finished` is false, where cancelled is not a failure), or when the lockout forces a goBack. Never send the PIN itself. This screen is opened by a caller, so the cancelled status stands in for a separate intent event. Properties: `action`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `attempts_failed`, `walletType`.

Restore wallet from cloud backup on `Routes.BACKUP_SHEET`; Enter backup password on `Routes.RESTORE_CLOUD_SHEET` (core) has no event. Answers how many restore attempts succeed and why they fail. Nothing records this today, only backup creation. It fires in RestoreCloudStep.onSubmit from the status of restoreCloudBackup, and from the catch branch for errors. The intent event backup_restore_started is also worth adding when the password is submitted, so drop-off before submit is measurable. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `cloud_platform`, `entry_point`, `is_first_wallet`.

Set up cash account on `Routes.CASH_DEPOSIT_INTRO_PANEL` (core) has no event. The intro view event and the phone submit event have nothing between them. This measures how many people who see the intro start setup, and how many are refused because the wallet is a hardware wallet. handleSetUpAccount shows an alert for hardware wallets before it navigates, which nothing else records. The same event also carries the sign-in and other-deposit-methods presses through the cta property. Properties: `cta`, `signup_enabled`, `blocked_reason`.

Search for and select a Ledger device on `Routes.PAIR_HARDWARE_WALLET_NAVIGATOR` (core) has no event. pair_hw_wallet_nav.entered and .exited show who starts and who leaves, but not whether a device was found and paired or what blocked it. It fires from useLedgerImport when the device pairs or the search errors. The intent is the existing nav entered event. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `flow_context`.

Enter a recipient and select an asset to send on `Routes.SEND_SHEET` (core) has no event. Sent transaction is the only outcome, and there is no event when the person picks an asset after entering a recipient. This lets you measure how many reach the amount step but never send. Entering a recipient is not a separate event because it only changes the form state. Properties: `asset_type`, `chain_id`, `recipient_type`, `is_sponsored_send`.

Add an account to an existing wallet group on `Routes.CHOOSE_WALLET_GROUP` (core) has no event. createAccountInExistingWallet never goes through createWallet, so wallet_create.succeeded and wallet_create.failed don't record it. This answers how many accounts users add to existing groups and how often it fails. The user can also cancel the naming modal, so an intent event is worth adding too. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `wallet_type`, `account_count_after`, `entry_point`.

Speed up a pending transaction on `Routes.SPEED_UP_AND_CANCEL_BOTTOM_SHEET`; Attempt to cancel a pending transaction on `Routes.SPEED_UP_AND_CANCEL_BOTTOM_SHEET`; Speed up a pending transaction on `Routes.SPEED_UP_AND_CANCEL_SHEET`; Attempt to cancel a pending transaction on `Routes.SPEED_UP_AND_CANCEL_SHEET` (core) has no event. Speed-up sends a new transaction with a failure path (catch around sendTransaction), and nothing records it. The number shows how often pending transactions get stuck and whether the replacement works. A transaction_replace_started intent event is worth adding too, since users can close the sheet. Properties: `replacement_type`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `chain_id`, `tx_gas_fee_type`, `is_hardware_wallet`, `entry_point`.

Switch wallet on `Routes.CHANGE_WALLET_SHEET` (core) has no event. Answers how often people switch between wallets and how many use more than one. Fires in onChangeAccount only when the switch actually proceeds, which excludes edit mode and a tap on the current address. The sheet's other events are taps on menu items, and none records the switch itself. Properties: `entry_point`, `wallet_count`, `is_watch_only_target`, `target_wallet_type`, `is_pinned`.

Start buying a market outcome on `Routes.POLYMARKET_MARKET_SHEET` (core) has no event. A buy can be abandoned: only `predictions.place_order` and its failed event exist, with nothing before them. This answers 'how many people open a buy and how many complete it, by entry point?'. The same name is sent from every place that opens the new-position sheet, with `entry_point` to tell them apart. Fire it when the new-position sheet opens. Properties: `event_slug`, `market_slug`, `outcome`, `outcome_index`, `entry_point`.

Select a cloud backup to restore on `Routes.VIEW_CLOUD_BACKUPS` (core) has no event. Answers how many people start restoring from a cloud backup, which backup they pick and how old it is. Selecting a backup opens the restore step and the restore can fail or be abandoned, so pair it with a `backup_restore_completed` outcome (`status`, `failure_reason`) if the plan has none. Properties: `entry_point`, `is_most_recent`, `backup_age_bucket`, `cloud_platform`, `backup_count`.

Revoke a network delegation on `Routes.VIEW_WALLET_DELEGATIONS` (core) has no event. Answers how often users disable smart-account delegation, on one network or all, and whether they leave a third-party delegation or Rainbow's own. The code only navigates to the revoke panel and nothing is tracked in the delegation feature, so also add the outcome `delegation_revoked` (`status`, `failure_reason`) from the panel. `revoke_reason` covers the single-network, third-party and disable-smart-wallet paths. Properties: `revoke_reason`, `delegation_type`, `chain_id`, `entry_point`.

Restore wallet from backup after wallet error on `Routes.WALLET_ERROR_SHEET` (core) has no event. Answers how many users who hit a broken keychain (passcode disabled, device changed) choose to restore versus dismiss. `action` is restore or dismiss, and `cause` and `resolution` come from the sheet's logic. The restore itself continues in the add-wallet flow. Properties: `cause`, `resolution`, `action`.

Deposit funds into perps account on `Routes.PERPS_DEPOSIT_SCREEN` (core) has no event. The perps deposit flow (PerpsDepositScreen using the shared DepositScreen and useDepositHandler) has no analytics, while withdrawals already have perps.withdrew and perps.withdraw.failed. This answers how many deposits succeed or fail, with what funding asset or chain, and whether sponsored gas helps. A deposit can fail or be abandoned, so a matching intent event (perps_deposit_started) is worth adding too. Send both from the perps-specific path, not from the shared funding system, so they aren't mixed with other deposit configs. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `failure_stage`, `amount_usd`, `from_asset_symbol`, `from_chain_id`, `execution_strategy`, `is_sponsored`, `is_first_deposit`.

Revoke smart wallet delegation on `Routes.REVOKE_DELEGATION_PANEL` (core) has no event. handleRevoke only logs, so nobody can count how many users disable their smart wallet or respond to a vulnerability alert, or how often it works. This is a money-safety flow where the number answers whether security alerts get acted on. The panel opening (intent) is worth adding too as delegation_revoke_started, so you can see users who open it and never confirm. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `revoke_reason`, `is_backend_triggered`, `chain_ids_count`, `failed_chain_count`, `is_retry`, `attempt_number`.

Save or edit a contact profile on `Routes.MODAL_SCREEN` (secondary) has no event. This answers how many contacts people save per week and from where. ContactProfileState.handleAddContact saves a contact only when the nickname is non-empty, and nothing records it today. It isn't a Wallet Profile modal tap, so no existing event covers it. Cancel and abandonment aren't worth a separate event: the modal has no start event, and an empty name never reaches the save. Properties: `entry_point`, `is_new_contact`, `has_ens`, `nickname_char_count`, `walletAddressHash`.

Remove linked card on `Routes.CASH_PAYMENT_METHODS_SHEET` (secondary) has no event. The plan has card linking events but nothing for removing the card. Churn from Cash and failed removals depend on it. It fires after cardRemovalFlowActions.remove resolves, from the confirm button. 'Keep card' is the abandon branch and is not worth its own event. Properties: `status`, `brand`.

Cancel a WalletConnect connection on `Routes.WALLET_CONNECT_APPROVAL_SHEET` (secondary) has no event. Shown Walletconnect session request has no outcome, so approval rate and abandonment can't be measured. This pairs with it: handleConnect gives approved, handleCancel gives rejected, and the unmount cleanup with handled false gives dismissed. Cancelled and dismissed are not failures. Properties: `status`, `dappName`, `dappUrl`, `request_type`, `chainId`, `wait_time_seconds`, `wallet_changed`, `network_changed`.

Enable or disable smart wallet on `Routes.VIEW_WALLET_DELEGATIONS` (secondary) has no event. It answers how many users turn the smart wallet on or off, and how many had active delegations to revoke when they did. Fire it where the preference actually changes: on delegation.enable/disable, and after the revoke success callback when disabling. Revoking has its own outcome in the revoke panel, so this event is not an intent/outcome pair. Properties: `action`, `address_hash`, `rainbow_delegation_count`, `revoked_networks`.
